title.zh: 卷一百八十六 志第一百三十九 食貨下八
title.raw: 卷一百八十六 志第一百三十九 食貨下八 Volume 186 Treatises 139: Finance and Economics 2h

sentences.zh: 食貨下八○商稅市易均輸互市舶法

translations.literal: Finance and Economics, Part 8 ○ Commercial Taxation, the Market Purchase System, Balanced Transport, Mutual Border Trade, and Maritime Trade Law
translations.idiomatic: Finance and Economics, Part 8: Commercial Taxes, the Market Purchase System, Balanced Transport, Border Markets, and Maritime Trade Regulations

sentences.zh: 商稅凡州縣皆置務，關鎮亦或有之；

translations.literal: For commercial taxes, every prefecture and county established tax offices, and pass towns sometimes had them as well;
translations.idiomatic: Commercial tax offices were set up in every prefecture and county, and in some cases at passes and market towns as well.

sentences.zh: 大則專置官監臨，小則令、佐兼領；

translations.literal: In large ones dedicated officials were specially appointed to supervise; in small ones magistrates and assistants concurrently managed them;
translations.idiomatic: Larger stations had officials appointed solely to supervise them, while smaller ones were overseen concurrently by magistrates and their assistants.

sentences.zh: 諸州仍令都監、監押同掌。

translations.literal: In the various prefectures the chief military inspectors and prison wardens were still ordered to share administration.
translations.idiomatic: In the prefectures as well, chief military inspectors and prison wardens were directed to share in the administration.

sentences.zh: 行者齎貨，謂之「過稅」，每千錢算二十；

translations.literal: For travelers carrying goods, it was called "transit tax," calculated at twenty per thousand cash;
translations.idiomatic: Goods carried by traveling merchants were subject to a "transit tax" of twenty cash per thousand.

sentences.zh: 居者市鬻，謂之「住稅」，每千錢算三十，大約如此。

translations.literal: For residents trading in the market, it was called "residence tax," calculated at thirty per thousand cash—approximately thus.
translations.idiomatic: Goods sold by resident merchants in the market were subject to a "residence tax" of thirty cash per thousand—roughly the standard rate.

sentences.zh: 然無定制，其名物各隨地宜而不一焉。

translations.literal: Yet there was no fixed regulation; the named goods each followed local suitability and were not uniform.
translations.idiomatic: However, there were no fixed rules nationwide; the list of taxable goods varied with local conditions.

sentences.zh: 行旅齎裝，非有貨幣當算者，無得發篋搜索。

translations.literal: For travelers' baggage, when there were no goods or currency subject to assessment, trunk-searching was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Officials were forbidden to break open travelers' baggage unless goods or currency liable to taxation were involved.

sentences.zh: 凡販夫販婦細碎交易，嶺南商賈齎生藥及民間所織縑帛，非鬻於市者皆勿算。

translations.literal: All peddlers' petty transactions, Lingnan merchants carrying raw medicines, and silk cloth woven by the populace that was not sold in the market were all not to be assessed.
translations.idiomatic: Petty dealings by street vendors, medicinal herbs brought by Lingnan merchants, and household-woven silks not offered for market sale were all exempt from taxation.

sentences.zh: 常稅名物，令有司件析頒行天下，揭於版，置官署屋壁，俾其遵守。

translations.literal: Regular-tax named goods: officials were ordered to itemize and promulgate them throughout the realm, posted on boards and placed on government office walls so that all would comply.
translations.idiomatic: The roster of regularly taxed commodities was itemized by the authorities, promulgated empire-wide, and posted on boards in government offices so that all would observe it.

sentences.zh: 應算物貨而輒藏匿，為官司所捕獲，沒其三分之一，以半畀捕者。

translations.literal: Goods liable to taxation that were deliberately concealed, when captured by government agents, had one-third confiscated, half of which was given to the captor.
translations.idiomatic: If taxable goods were deliberately concealed and seized by officials, one-third of the goods was confiscated and half of that share was given to whoever reported the offense.

sentences.zh: 販鬻而不由官路者罪之。

translations.literal: Those who sold goods without using official routes were punished.
translations.idiomatic: Merchants who traded without using official routes were subject to punishment.

sentences.zh: 有官須者十取其一，謂之「抽稅」。

translations.literal: For goods the government needed, one in ten was taken, called "withholding tax."
translations.idiomatic: Where the government required certain commodities, a tenth was levied, called the "withholding tax."

sentences.zh: 自唐室藩鎮多便宜從事，擅其征利，以及五季，諸國益務掊聚財貨以自贍，故征算尤繁。

translations.literal: From the Tang, when military governors often acted expediently at will and monopolized levies and profits, through the Five Dynasties, when the various states increasingly strove to gouge and amass valuables to support themselves, hence tax assessments were especially numerous.
translations.idiomatic: From the Tang, when military governors often acted on their own authority and kept levy profits for themselves, through the Five Dynasties, when rival states increasingly squeezed the populace to finance themselves, commercial taxation grew especially heavy.

sentences.zh: 宋興，所下之國，必詔蠲省，屢敕官吏毋事煩苛、規羨餘以徼恩寵。

translations.literal: When the Song arose, in every state they subdued they invariably issued edicts to reduce and cut taxes, repeatedly ordering officials not to be vexatious and harsh or scheme for surplus profits to seek favor and reward.
translations.idiomatic: When the Song dynasty was founded, edicts to lighten taxation were issued in every region they brought under control, and officials were repeatedly warned not to harass the people or inflate revenues to court imperial favor.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符六年，始免諸路州軍農器之稅。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Dazhong Xiangfu, the tax on agricultural implements in all circuit prefectures and armies was first exempted.
translations.idiomatic: In 1013, taxes on agricultural tools were abolished throughout the empire.

sentences.zh: 諸州津渡舊皆有算，或水涸改置橋梁，有司猶責主者備償。

translations.literal: Ferry crossings in the various prefectures formerly all had toll assessments; when water dried up and bridges were built instead, officials still charged those in charge to make compensation.
translations.idiomatic: Ferry crossings in the prefectures had long been subject to tolls; even when drought forced relocation of crossings to bridges, officials still demanded reimbursement from those responsible.

sentences.zh: 建隆初，詔除滄、德、棣、淄、齊、鄆幹渡三十九處算錢，水漲聽民置渡，勿收其算。

translations.literal: Early in Jianlong, an edict abolished toll monies at thirty-nine dry crossings in Cang, De, Di, Zi, Qi, and Yun prefectures; when waters rose the people were permitted to set up ferries without collecting tolls.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the reign, tolls were abolished at thirty-nine dry crossings in six Hebei prefectures, and when floods rose the people were allowed to operate ferries without paying tolls.

sentences.zh: 自是，有類此者多因恩宥蠲除。

translations.literal: From this time, many similar cases were often remitted through imperial grace.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, many similar levies were waived by imperial grace.

sentences.zh: 其餘橘園、魚池、水磑、社酒、蓮藕、鵝鴨、螺蚌、柴薪、地鋪、枯牛骨、溉田水利等名，皆因諸國舊制，前後屢詔廢省。

translations.literal: The rest—orange groves, fish ponds, water mills, communal wine, lotus roots, geese and ducks, snails and mussels, firewood, ground mats, dried ox bones, irrigation works, and the like—were all due to former states' old systems; edicts repeatedly abolished and cut them before and after.
translations.idiomatic: Taxes on orange groves, fish ponds, water mills, communal wine, lotus roots, poultry, shellfish, firewood, ground-rent stalls, dried ox bones, irrigation works, and the like—all legacies of the former states—were repeatedly abolished by imperial edict.

sentences.zh: 緣河州縣民船載粟亦輸算，三年，始罷。

translations.literal: Along the Yellow River, county and prefecture civilian boats carrying grain also paid assessments; after three years this was first abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Grain boats on the Yellow River had also been taxed; after three years this levy was finally ended.

sentences.zh: 天聖以來，國用浸廣，有請算緡錢以助經費者。

translations.literal: Since Tiansheng, state expenditures gradually expanded, and there were proposals to assess strings of cash to assist expenses.
translations.idiomatic: From the Tiansheng era onward, as state expenditures grew, some proposed taxing copper cash to bolster the treasury.

sentences.zh: 仁宗曰：「貨泉之利，欲流天下通有無，何可算也？」

translations.literal: Emperor Renzong said: "The profit of currency is meant to circulate throughout the realm and connect surplus with shortage—how can it be assessed?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Renzong said, "Money is meant to circulate throughout the realm and balance abundance and scarcity—how can we tax it?"

sentences.zh: 一日，內出蜀羅一端，為印朱所漬者數重，因詔天下稅務，毋輒汙壞商人物帛。

translations.literal: One day, from within the palace a length of Shu silk was produced, stained in several layers by seal vermilion, and accordingly an edict was sent to tax offices throughout the realm not to deface or ruin merchants' goods and cloth.
translations.idiomatic: One day the palace produced a length of Shu silk ruined by repeated stampings of sealing vermilion, and the emperor accordingly ordered tax offices empire-wide not to deface merchants' goods and textiles.

sentences.zh: 康定元年，西邊兵費不給，州縣或增所算名物，朝廷知之，悉命蠲去。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kangding, western frontier military expenses were insufficient, and some prefectures and counties increased listed taxable goods; when the court learned of this, it ordered all such increases abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In 1040, when western frontier military costs ran short, some localities expanded their lists of taxable goods; once the court learned of this, it ordered all such increases repealed.

sentences.zh: 既而下詔敕勵，且戒毋搜索行者家屬，歲儉則免算耕牛，水鄉又或弛蒲、魚、果、蓏之稅，民流而渡河者亦為之免算。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward edicts encouraging restraint were issued, also warning against searching travelers' families; in lean years plow oxen were exempted from assessment; in water districts taxes on reeds, fish, fruit, and melons were sometimes relaxed; people fleeing famine who crossed rivers were also exempted from assessment.
translations.idiomatic: Edicts soon followed urging restraint and forbidding searches of travelers' families; plow oxen were exempted in famine years; water districts sometimes saw taxes on reeds, fish, fruit, and melons relaxed; and refugees crossing rivers were also exempted.

sentences.zh: 應算而匿不自言者，雖聽人捕告，抵罪如舊法，然須物皆見在乃聽，以防誣罔。

translations.literal: Those liable to assessment who concealed without reporting—although people were permitted to apprehend and inform, punishment followed the old law—yet it was required that the goods all be present before proceedings were permitted, to guard against false accusation.
translations.idiomatic: Concealing taxable goods without reporting remained punishable under the old law, and informants were still rewarded; but proceedings were allowed only when the goods were actually present, to prevent false denunciation.

sentences.zh: 至於歲課贏縮，屢詔有司裁定，前後以詔蠲放者，不可勝數。

translations.literal: As for annual revenue surpluses and shortfalls, the court repeatedly ordered officials to fix quotas; remissions by edict before and after were innumerable.
translations.idiomatic: When annual tax quotas proved too high or too low, the court repeatedly ordered adjustments, and imperial remissions over the years were beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 皇祐中，歲課緡錢七百八十六萬三千九百。

translations.literal: In the Huangyou period, annual revenue in strings of cash was 7,863,900.
translations.idiomatic: During the Huangyou era (1049–1054), annual commercial tax revenue reached 7,863,900 strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 嘉祐以後，弛茶禁，所曆州縣收算錢。

translations.literal: After Jiayou, the tea monopoly was relaxed, and prefectures and counties traversed collected assessment monies.
translations.idiomatic: After the Jiayou era, when the tea monopoly was relaxed, prefectures and counties along trade routes collected transit taxes instead.

sentences.zh: 至治平中，歲課增六十餘萬，而茶稅錢居四十九萬八千六百。

translations.literal: By the Zhiping period, annual revenue increased by more than 600,000, of which tea tax monies accounted for 498,600.
translations.idiomatic: By the Zhiping era, annual receipts had risen by more than 600,000 strings, of which tea duties alone contributed 498,600.

sentences.zh: 熙寧以來，河北、河東、陝西三路支移，民以租賦齎貨至邊貿易以輸官者，勿稅；

translations.literal: Since Xining, in the Hebei, Hedong, and Shaanxi circuits for relocation tax deliveries, when the people brought rent and tax goods to the frontier to trade and deliver to the government, they were not taxed;
translations.idiomatic: From the Xining reforms onward, people in the Hebei, Hedong, and Shaanxi circuits who transported rent grain and tax goods to the frontier for official trade were exempt from commercial tax;

sentences.zh: 河北流民復業者所過免算。

translations.literal: displaced persons from Hebei returning to their occupations were exempted from assessments along the way.
translations.idiomatic: refugees from Hebei returning to farming were also exempt from transit duties along the route.

sentences.zh: 後以歲稔，慮逸稅課，復舊。

translations.literal: Later, because harvests were good, fearing lost tax quotas, the old rules were restored.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when harvests improved and officials feared lost revenue, the exemptions were revoked.

sentences.zh: 五年，以在京商稅院隸提舉市易務。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, the capital commercial tax office was placed under the Market Purchase Commission.
translations.idiomatic: In 1072, the capital commercial tax office was placed under the Market Purchase Commission.

sentences.zh: 七年，減國門之稅數十種，錢不滿三十者蠲之。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, dozens of types of capital gate taxes were reduced; amounts under thirty cash were exempted.
translations.idiomatic: In 1074, dozens of capital gate levies were cut, and amounts under thirty cash were waived entirely.

sentences.zh: 其先，外城二十門皆責以課息，近令隨閑、要分等，以檢捕獲失之數為賞罰；

translations.literal: Earlier, all twenty outer city gates were charged with revenue quotas; recently they were ordered to grade by busy and quiet, rewards and punishments based on numbers of seizures and losses detected;
translations.idiomatic: Previously all twenty outer city gates had been assigned revenue targets; now they were graded by traffic volume, with rewards and penalties tied to seizure records;

sentences.zh: 既而以歲旱，復有是命。

translations.literal: afterward, because of drought year, that order was again issued.
translations.idiomatic: when drought struck, that easing order was reissued.

sentences.zh: 元豐元年，濱、棣、滄州竹木、魚果、炭箔稅不及百錢者蠲之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanfeng, in Bin, Di, and Cang prefectures taxes on bamboo, wood, fish, fruit, charcoal, and foil under one hundred cash were exempted.
translations.idiomatic: In 1078, in coastal prefectures, commercial taxes on bamboo, timber, fish, fruit, charcoal, and foil amounting to less than one hundred cash were abolished.

sentences.zh: 二年，熙河路製置邊防財用李憲擅榷本路商貨，令漕臣蔣之奇劾其罪。

translations.literal: In the second year, Li Xian, Commissioner of Frontier Financial Affairs for the Xining Circuit, on his own authority monopolized commercial goods of that circuit; the transport commissioner Jiang Zhiqi was ordered to impeach him.
translations.idiomatic: In 1079, Li Xian, commissioner for frontier finances on the Xining Circuit, was impeached for imposing a monopoly on local commerce without authorization.

sentences.zh: 導洛通汴司請置堆垛場於泗州，賈物至者，先入官場，官以船運至京，稍輸船算。

translations.literal: The Directorate Guiding the Luo into the Bian requested setting up stacking yards at Sizhou; when merchants' goods arrived they first entered the government yard, the government shipped them by boat to the capital, and paid a slight boat tax.
translations.idiomatic: The agency overseeing the Luo–Bian canal proposed stacking yards at Sizhou where goods would enter government warehouses before shipment to the capital, with a modest boat duty charged.

sentences.zh: 明年，詔：近京以通津水門外順成倉為場。

translations.literal: The next year, an edict: near the capital, outside Tongjin Water Gate at Shuncheng granary was designated as the yard.
translations.idiomatic: The following year an edict designated the Shuncheng granary outside Tongjin Water Gate near the capital as the site.

sentences.zh: 非導洛司船而載商稅入汴者，許糾告，雖自請稅，猶如私載法。

translations.literal: For boats not of the Guiding Luo office carrying commercial-tax goods into the Bian, informing was permitted; even if they voluntarily requested taxation, they were still treated under the private carriage law.
translations.idiomatic: Carrying taxed merchandise into the Bian on unauthorized boats was subject to denunciation; even voluntary payment of duties did not spare violators penalties for clandestine transport.

sentences.zh: 惟日用物非販易，若廢箔、柴草、竹木之類勿禁。

translations.literal: Only daily-use goods not for trade, such as waste foil, firewood, grass, bamboo, and wood, were not forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Daily necessities not intended for trade—waste materials, firewood, grass, bamboo, and timber—were exempt from the ban.

sentences.zh: 瓊管奏：「海南收稅，較船之丈尺，謂之『格納』。

translations.literal: The Qiong administration memorialized: "In Hainan tax collection measured the boat's dimensions, called 'graded assessment.
translations.idiomatic: The Qiongzhou administration reported: "In Hainan, taxes were assessed by measuring a ship's dimensions, a method called 'graded assessment.

sentences.zh: 其法分三等，有所較無幾，而輸錢多寡十倍。

translations.literal: The method divided three grades; sometimes what was measured was little, yet monies paid differed tenfold.
translations.idiomatic: The method used three grades, so that ships of similar size could pay ten times as much in tax.

sentences.zh: 賈物自泉、福、兩浙、湖、廣至者，皆金銀物帛，直或至萬餘緡；

translations.literal: Merchandise arriving from Quan, Fu, the two Zhe circuits, Hu, and Guang were all gold, silver, goods, and silks, worth sometimes more than ten thousand strings;
translations.idiomatic: Goods from Quanzhou, Fuzhou, the two Zhe circuits, Hunan, and Guangdong were mostly gold, silver, and silks worth as much as ten thousand strings;

sentences.zh: 自高、化至者，唯米包、瓦器、牛畜之類，直才百一，而概收以丈尺。

translations.literal: Those from Gao and Hua were only rice sacks, pottery, cattle, and the like, worth only one-hundredth as much, yet were taxed in bulk by measurement.
translations.idiomatic: Ships from Gaozhou and Huazhou carried only rice sacks, pottery, and livestock worth a hundredth as much, yet were taxed by hull measurement alone.

sentences.zh: 故高、化商人不至，海南遂乏牛米。

translations.literal: Therefore merchants from Gao and Hua did not come, and Hainan consequently lacked rice and cattle.
translations.idiomatic: Merchants from Gaozhou and Huazhou therefore stopped coming, and Hainan was left short of grain and cattle.

sentences.zh: 請自今用物貴賤多寡計稅，官給文憑，聽鬻於部內，否則許糾告，以船貨給賞。」

translations.literal: We request that from now on tax be calculated by the value and quantity of goods, the government issue certificates, and permit sale within the circuit; otherwise informing is permitted, with ship cargo given as reward."
translations.idiomatic: We ask that hereafter tax be assessed on the value and quantity of goods, that officials issue certificates permitting sale within the circuit, and that informants be rewarded with a share of the ship's cargo."

sentences.zh: 詔如所奏。

translations.literal: An edict approved the memorial as submitted.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved the proposal.

sentences.zh: 六年，京東漕臣吳居厚言：「商人負正稅七萬六千餘緡，倍稅十五萬二千餘緡。」

translations.literal: In the sixth year, the Jingdong transport commissioner Wu Ju Hou said: "Merchants owe regular tax of more than 76,000 strings, and double tax of more than 152,000 strings."
translations.idiomatic: In 1083, the Jingdong transport commissioner Wu Juhou reported: "Merchants owe regular taxes of more than 76,000 strings and penalty taxes at double rate of more than 152,000 strings."

sentences.zh: 詔蠲其倍稅，納正稅，百千以下期以三年，百千以上五年。

translations.literal: An edict remitted their double tax; they were to pay regular tax, amounts under one hundred strings within three years, one hundred and above within five.
translations.idiomatic: The court remitted the penalty taxes and required payment of regular taxes only, with three years allowed for amounts under one hundred strings and five years for larger sums.

sentences.zh: 元祐元年，戶部請令在京商稅院，酌取元豐八年錢五十五萬二千二百六十一緡有奇，以為新額，自明年始。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanyou, the Ministry of Revenue requested that the capital commercial tax office take the Yuanfeng eighth-year figure of 552,261-odd strings as the new quota, effective from the next year.
translations.idiomatic: In 1086, the Ministry of Revenue asked that the capital commercial tax office adopt the 1085 revenue of 552,261 strings as its new annual quota, effective the following year.

sentences.zh: 三年，又以天聖歲課為額，蓋戶部用五年並增之法，立額既重，歲課不登，故言者論而更之。

translations.literal: In the third year, the Tiansheng annual revenue was again taken as the quota, for the Ministry of Revenue had used the method of five-year combined increases; quotas once set too high, annual revenue could not be met, so critics argued and it was changed.
translations.idiomatic: In 1088, the quota was reset to the Tiansheng-era level, because the Ministry's method of averaging five years of increases had set targets too high for revenue to meet, prompting critics to demand revision.

sentences.zh: 七年，罷諸路承買土產稅場。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, contracted purchase of local products tax stations in all circuits was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In 1092, the system of contracting out local-product tax stations was abolished empire-wide.

sentences.zh: 初，罷江南路承買，而河東轉運司以為較元祐六年官鹽額增三萬餘緡，遂行之諸路。

translations.literal: At first, contracted purchase in the Jiangnan circuit was abolished, but the Hedong transport commission held that compared with the Yuanyou sixth-year official salt quota it increased by more than 30,000 strings, and so it was extended to all circuits.
translations.idiomatic: Initially the Jiangnan circuit ended contracting, but the Hedong transport commission reported that official salt revenue had risen by more than 30,000 strings compared with 1091, and the practice was extended to all circuits.

sentences.zh: 八年，權蠲商人載米入京糶賣力勝之稅。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, the capacity-surplus tax on merchants bringing rice to the capital for sale was temporarily remitted.
translations.idiomatic: In 1093, the capacity-surplus tax on grain merchants shipping rice to the capital for sale was temporarily waived.

sentences.zh: 先是，熙寧六年，蘇、湖歲稔，穀價比淮南十五，而商船以力勝稅不至，嘗命權蠲。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the sixth year of Xining, Suzhou and Huzhou had good harvests; grain prices were one-fifteenth those south of the Huai, yet merchant boats did not come because of the capacity-surplus tax, and a temporary remission was once ordered.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, in 1073, when Suzhou and Huzhou had bumper harvests and grain sold for one-fifteenth the price in Huainan, merchant ships stayed away because of the capacity-surplus tax, and a temporary waiver had been ordered.

sentences.zh: 惠止一方，未為定法。

translations.literal: The benefit stopped at one region and did not become a fixed regulation.
translations.idiomatic: The relief applied only locally and was never made permanent law.

sentences.zh: 及汴泗垛場法行，穀船毋得增置，而力勝之稅益三之一。

translations.literal: When the Bian and Si stacking-yard regulations took effect, grain boats could not be added, and the capacity-surplus tax increased by one-third.
translations.idiomatic: When the Bian and Si stacking-yard regulations took effect, no additional grain boats were permitted, and the capacity-surplus tax was raised by one-third.

sentences.zh: 至是，蘇軾言：「法不稅五穀，請削去力勝錢之條，而行天聖免稅之制。」

translations.literal: At this time Su Shi said: "The law does not tax the five grains; we request deleting the capacity-surplus money provision and implementing the Tiansheng tax-exemption system."
translations.idiomatic: At this point Su Shi argued: "The law exempts grain from taxation; I ask that the capacity-surplus levy be abolished and the Tiansheng-era exemption restored."

sentences.zh: 既而尚書省亦言在京穀貴，欲平其直，復權蠲之。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward the Secretariat also said grain in the capital was dear and they wished to level its price, and temporarily remitted it again.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat soon added that grain in the capital was costly and that prices should be stabilized, and the tax was temporarily waived again.

sentences.zh: 後徽宗宣和中，以州縣災傷並贍給都下，亦一再免，旋復如舊；

translations.literal: Later in Emperor Huizong's Xuanhe period, because of disaster damage in prefectures and counties and relief for the capital, it was also repeatedly exempted, then soon restored as before;
translations.idiomatic: Later, during Emperor Huizong's Xuanhe reign, the tax was waived more than once to relieve disaster-stricken regions and supply the capital, then soon restored;

sentences.zh: 惟兩浙並東北鹽，以鹽事司之請，遂不復徵。

translations.literal: only for the two Zhe circuits and northeastern salt, at the Salt Affairs Commission's request, it was no longer levied.
translations.idiomatic: only for the two Zhe circuits and northeastern salt regions, at the Salt Commission's request, was the levy permanently discontinued.

sentences.zh: 自哲宗即位，罷導洛物貨場。

translations.literal: From Emperor Zhezong's accession, the Guiding Luo goods yard was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhezong came to the throne, the Guiding Luo goods depot was abolished.

sentences.zh: 紹聖四年，藍從熙提舉京城所，欲復其事，令泗州及京師洛口各置垛場，並請復麵市、牛羊圈。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Shaosheng, Lan Congxi, commissioner of the Capital Office, wished to restore the matter, ordering stacking yards set up at Sizhou and Luokou in the capital, and also requesting restoration of the flour market and cattle and sheep pens.
translations.idiomatic: In 1097, Lan Congxi, commissioner of the Capital Office, sought to revive the system, proposing stacking yards at Sizhou and Luokou in the capital and restoration of the flour market and livestock pens.

sentences.zh: 詔下尚書省，久之遂寢。

translations.literal: An edict was sent down to the Secretariat; after a long time the matter was shelved.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was referred to the Secretariat and eventually shelved.

sentences.zh: 至是，提舉汴河堤岸王憲復言之，且請假溫、明州運船給用。

translations.literal: At this time Wang Xian, commissioner of Bian River embankments, raised it again, and also requested borrowing transport boats from Wen and Ming prefectures for use.
translations.idiomatic: At this point Wang Xian, commissioner of Bian River embankments, revived the proposal and asked to borrow transport vessels from Wenzhou and Mingzhou.

sentences.zh: 命太府少卿鄭僅同詳度。

translations.literal: The Vice Minister of the Palace Storehouse Zheng Jin was ordered to deliberate jointly.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister Zheng Jin of the Palace Storehouse was ordered to review the plan jointly.

sentences.zh: 明年，竟詔勿行。

translations.literal: The next year, an edict was finally issued not to implement it.
translations.idiomatic: The following year an edict finally ordered that it not be carried out.

sentences.zh: 五年，令戶部取天下稅務五年所收之數，酌多寡為中制，頒諸路揭版示之，率十年一易；

translations.literal: In the fifth year, the Ministry of Revenue was ordered to take five years of receipts from tax offices throughout the realm, adjust high and low to a middle standard, promulgate to all circuits on posted boards, generally changing every ten years;
translations.idiomatic: In 1111, the Ministry of Revenue was ordered to average five years of tax receipts empire-wide into moderate quotas, post them on boards in every circuit, and revise them roughly every ten years;

sentences.zh: 其增名額及多稅者，並論以違制。

translations.literal: those who increased listed items or over-taxed were all prosecuted for violation of regulations.
translations.idiomatic: officials who added tax categories or over-collected were to be prosecuted for violating regulations.

sentences.zh: 大觀元年，凡典買牛畜、舟車之類未印契者，更期以百日，免倍稅。

translations.literal: In the first year of Daguan, for all pawned purchase of cattle, boats, carts, and the like without stamped contracts, a further grace of one hundred days was granted, exempting double tax.
translations.idiomatic: In 1107, contracts for pawned sales of livestock and vehicles without official seals were given a further hundred-day grace period exempt from penalty tax.

sentences.zh: 二年，詔在京諸門，凡民衣屨、穀菽、雞魚、蔬果、柴炭、瓷瓦器之類，並蠲其稅；

translations.literal: In the second year, an edict: at all capital gates, commoners' clothing, shoes, grain, beans, chickens, fish, vegetables, fruit, firewood, charcoal, porcelain, and tiles were all to have their taxes remitted;
translations.idiomatic: In 1108, an edict exempted at all capital gates taxes on everyday goods such as clothing, grain, poultry, fish, produce, fuel, and pottery;

sentences.zh: 歲終計所蠲數，令大觀庫給償。

translations.literal: at year's end the remitted amount was calculated and the Daguan treasury ordered to provide compensation.
translations.idiomatic: at year's end the remitted amounts were calculated and reimbursed from the Daguan treasury.

sentences.zh: 宣和二年，宮觀、寺院、臣僚之家商販，令關津搜閱，如元豐法輸稅，歲終以次數報轉運司取旨。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xuanhe, commercial trade by Daoist abbeys, Buddhist temples, and officials' households: passes and ferries were ordered to search and inspect; like the Yuanfeng law they paid tax; at year's end counts were reported in order to transport commissions for imperial decision.
translations.idiomatic: In 1120, commercial trade conducted by Daoist temples, Buddhist monasteries, and officials' households was ordered searched at passes and ferries and taxed under the Yuanfeng regulations, with annual reports to transport commissions for imperial approval.

sentences.zh: 初，元符令，品官供家服用物免稅。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Yuanfu regulation exempted ranked officials' household goods for personal use from tax.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Yuanfu regulations, ranked officials' household goods for personal use had been tax-exempt.

sentences.zh: 至建中靖國初，馬、牛、駝、驢、騾已不入服用例，而比年臣僚營私牟利者眾，宮觀寺院多有專降免稅之旨，皆以船艘賈販，故有是詔。

translations.literal: By the beginning of Jianzhong Jingguo, horses, cattle, camels, donkeys, and mules were no longer within the personal-use category, yet in recent years many officials pursued private profit; Daoist abbeys and temples often had special edicts exempting tax—all engaged in trade by boat—hence this edict.
translations.idiomatic: By the Jianzhong Jingguo era, horses, cattle, and pack animals no longer qualified as personal-use goods, yet many officials had turned to private trade; temples and monasteries often held special tax exemptions—all shipping goods by boat—hence this edict.

sentences.zh: 漕臣劉既濟起應奉物，兩浙、淮南等路稅例外，增一分以供費；

translations.literal: The transport commissioner Liu Jiji raised tribute goods; in the two Zhe circuits, Huainan, and other circuits, beyond regular tax, one-tenth more was added to supply expenses;
translations.idiomatic: Transport commissioner Liu Jiji raised tribute goods; in the two Zhe circuits, Huainan, and elsewhere an extra tenth was added to regular taxes to cover expenses;

sentences.zh: 三年，詔罷之。

translations.literal: In the third year, an edict abolished it.
translations.idiomatic: In 1121, an edict abolished the surcharge.

sentences.zh: 凡以蠶織農具、耕牛至兩浙、江東者，給文憑蠲稅一年。

translations.literal: All who brought sericulture goods, farm tools, and plow oxen to the two Zhe circuits and Jiangdong were given certificates exempting tax for one year.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone bringing silkworms, farm tools, or plow oxen to the two Zhe circuits and Jiangdong received a one-year tax exemption certificate.

sentences.zh: 四年，令諸路近歲所增稅錢，悉歸應奉司。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, recent years' increased tax monies in all circuits were ordered to go entirely to the Tribute Service.
translations.idiomatic: In 1122, all recent tax increases in every circuit were ordered diverted to the Tribute Service.

sentences.zh: 七年，以歲歉之後，用物少而民艱食，在京及畿內油、炭、麵、布、絮稅並力勝錢並權免。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, after lean harvest years when goods were few and the people had difficulty eating, in the capital and inner circuits taxes on oil, charcoal, flour, cloth, and cotton wadding, together with capacity-surplus monies, were all temporarily exempted.
translations.idiomatic: In 1125, after poor harvests when goods were scarce and food costly, taxes on oil, charcoal, flour, cloth, and cotton in the capital and surrounding circuits, along with capacity-surplus levies, were all temporarily waived.

sentences.zh: 提舉京東常平楊連奏：「 本路牛價貴，田多荒萊，請令販牛至本路者，仍給文憑蠲稅，俟二年足如舊。」

translations.literal: The Jingdong Ever-Normal commissioner Yang Lian memorialized: "In this circuit cattle prices are high and fields mostly lie fallow; we request that those selling cattle to this circuit still be given certificates exempting tax until after two years supply is restored as before."
translations.idiomatic: Jingdong Ever-Normal commissioner Yang Lian reported: "Cattle are costly in this circuit and much land lies fallow; I ask that merchants bringing cattle here continue to receive tax exemption certificates until the supply is restored in two years."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: Approval was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved.

sentences.zh: 靖康元年詔：「都城物價未平，凡稅物，權更蠲稅一年。」

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingkang an edict: "Capital prices are not yet stable; for all taxed goods, temporarily remit tax for one more year."
translations.idiomatic: In 1126 an edict declared: "Prices in the capital remain unsettled; all commercial taxes are temporarily waived for one more year."

sentences.zh: 臣僚上言：「祖宗舊制並政和新令，場務立額之法，並以五年增虧數較之，並增者取中數，並虧者取最高數，以為新額，故課息易給而商旅可通。

translations.literal: Officials memorialized: "The ancestral old system and Zhenghe new regulations for setting station quotas both compared five years of increase and deficit figures; where all increased, take the middle number; where all decreased, take the highest number, as the new quota—thus revenue was easy to meet and merchants and travelers could pass.
translations.idiomatic: Officials argued: "Under ancestral regulations and the Zhenghe reforms, tax-station quotas were set by comparing five years of receipts; when all years rose, the middle figure was taken; when all fell, the highest was taken—making quotas attainable and trade unimpeded.

sentences.zh: 近諸路轉運司不循其法，有益無損，致物價騰踴，官課愈負。

translations.literal: Recently transport commissions in various circuits did not follow this method, always increasing without decreasing, causing prices to soar and official revenue ever more in deficit.
translations.idiomatic: Recently transport commissions have ignored this method, raising quotas without ever lowering them, driving prices up while official revenue falls ever further short.

sentences.zh: 請令諸路提刑下諸郡，準舊法厘正立額。」

translations.literal: We request ordering judicial commissioners in all circuits to send down to all prefectures and rectify quotas according to the old law."
translations.idiomatic: We ask that judicial commissioners in every circuit order prefectures to reset quotas according to the old law."

sentences.zh: 詔依所奏。

translations.literal: An edict approved the memorial.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved.

sentences.zh: 高宗建炎元年詔，販貨上京者免稅。

translations.literal: In Emperor Gaozong's first year of Jianyan, an edict exempted those selling goods to the capital from tax.
translations.idiomatic: In 1127, Emperor Gaozong exempted merchants bringing goods to the capital from taxation.

sentences.zh: 明年又詔，販糧草入京抑稅者罪之；

translations.literal: The next year another edict: those who sold grain and fodder to the capital and suppressed tax were punished;
translations.idiomatic: The following year another edict punished anyone who under-taxed grain and fodder brought to the capital;

sentences.zh: 凡殘破州縣免竹木、磚瓦稅，北來歸正人及兩淮復業者亦免路稅。

translations.literal: all ravaged prefectures and counties were exempted from bamboo, wood, brick, and tile taxes; northerners coming to submit and those restoring livelihoods in the two Huai regions were also exempted from road tax.
translations.idiomatic: ravaged prefectures were exempted from taxes on timber and building materials; northerners who defected and those restoring farms on the two Huai were also exempted from road duties.

sentences.zh: 紹興三年，臨安火，免竹木稅。

translations.literal: In the third year of Shaoxing, after a fire in Lin'an, bamboo and wood taxes were exempted.
translations.idiomatic: In 1133, after a fire in Lin'an, taxes on timber were waived.

sentences.zh: 然當時都邑未奠，兵革未息，四方之稅，間有增置，及於江灣浦口量收海船稅，凡官司回易亦並收稅；

translations.literal: Yet at that time the capital was not yet settled, warfare had not ceased, taxes in the four directions were sometimes added, extending to measuring and collecting sea-ship taxes at Jiangwan and Pukou; all government agencies' trading ventures were also taxed;
translations.idiomatic: Yet the capital was not yet secure and warfare continued; taxes were sometimes added across the realm, including sea-ship duties at Jiangwan and Pukou, and even government trading ventures were taxed;

sentences.zh: 而寬弛之令亦錯見焉，如諸路增置之稅場，山間迂僻之縣鎮，經理未定之州郡，悉罷而免之。

translations.literal: yet lenient and relaxed orders also appeared in alternation, such as newly added tax stations in various circuits, remote mountain county towns, and prefectures whose administration was not yet settled—all abolished and exempted.
translations.idiomatic: yet lenient measures also appeared in turn, abolishing newly added tax stations, remote mountain market towns, and prefectures not yet fully administered.

sentences.zh: 又以稅網太密，減並者一百三十四，罷者九，免過稅者五，至於牛、米、薪、麵民間日用者並罷。

translations.literal: Because the tax net was too dense, 134 were reduced and merged, 9 abolished, 5 transit taxes exempted; as for cattle, rice, firewood, and flour for daily popular use, all were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Because the tax net was too dense, 134 stations were merged, 9 abolished, and 5 transit taxes waived; taxes on cattle, rice, firewood, flour, and other daily necessities were all ended.

sentences.zh: 孝宗繼誌，凡高宗省罷之未盡者，悉推行之；

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaozong continued the intent; all that Gaozong had reduced and abolished but not fully completed was thoroughly carried out;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaozong carried forward his predecessor's policy, fully implementing all tax reductions Gaozong had begun;

sentences.zh: 又以臨安府物價未平，免淳熙七年稅一半。

translations.literal: also because Lin'an prefecture's prices were not yet stable, half of the seventh year of Chunxi taxes was exempted.
translations.idiomatic: and because prices in Lin'an remained unsettled, half of the 1180 commercial taxes were waived.

sentences.zh: 光、寧以降，亦屢與放免商稅，或一年，或五月，或三月。

translations.literal: From the Guang and Ning reigns downward, commercial taxes were also repeatedly remitted, for one year, five months, or three months.
translations.idiomatic: From the Guang and Ning reigns onward, commercial taxes were also waived repeatedly—for a year, five months, or three months at a time.

sentences.zh: 凡遇火，放免竹木之稅亦然。

translations.literal: Whenever fire occurred, remission of bamboo and wood taxes was likewise granted.
translations.idiomatic: Timber taxes were likewise waived whenever fire broke out.

sentences.zh: 光、寧嗣服，諸郡稅額皆累有放免。

translations.literal: When Guang and Ning succeeded to the throne, tax quotas in all prefectures had repeated remissions.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Guang and Ning emperors, tax quotas in the prefectures were repeatedly reduced.

sentences.zh: 然當是時，雖寬大之旨屢頒，關市之征迭放，而貪吏並緣，苛取百出。

translations.literal: Yet at that time, although lenient intent was repeatedly promulgated and pass-market levies were repeatedly remitted, greedy officials exploited opportunities and harsh exactions appeared in hundreds of forms.
translations.idiomatic: Yet even as lenient edicts were repeatedly issued and market duties repeatedly waived, greedy officials seized every opportunity and invented countless harsh exactions.

sentences.zh: 私立稅場，算及緡錢、斗米、束薪、菜茹之屬，擅用稽察措置，添置專欄收檢。

translations.literal: They privately established tax stations, assessing strings of cash, piculs of rice, bundles of firewood, vegetables, and the like; they arbitrarily employed inspection measures and added special barriers for collection and inspection.
translations.idiomatic: They set up private tax stations, taxing strings of cash, piculs of rice, bundles of firewood, and vegetables, arbitrarily employing inspections and erecting special barriers to collect dues.

sentences.zh: 虛市有稅，空舟有稅，以食米為酒米，以衣服為布帛，皆有稅。

translations.literal: Empty markets had tax, empty boats had tax; treating food grain as wine grain, treating clothes as cloth and silk—all had tax.
translations.idiomatic: Empty markets were taxed, empty boats were taxed; grain was counted as wine, clothing as cloth—all were taxed.

sentences.zh: 遇士夫行李則搜囊發篋，目以興販。

translations.literal: Encountering scholars' baggage they searched bags and opened trunks, branding it as trade for profit.
translations.idiomatic: Scholar-officials' luggage was searched and trunks opened on the pretext of illicit trade.

sentences.zh: 甚者貧民貿易瑣細於村落，指為漏稅，輒加以罪。

translations.literal: In extreme cases poor people trading trifles in villages were pointed out as evading tax and immediately punished.
translations.idiomatic: In extreme cases poor villagers trading trifles were accused of tax evasion and immediately punished.

sentences.zh: 空身行旅，亦白取百金，方紆路避之，則欄截叫呼；

translations.literal: Travelers with empty persons also had to pay a hundred cash white levy; only when they took a detour to avoid it were they intercepted and shouted at;
translations.idiomatic: Even travelers carrying nothing were forced to pay a hundred cash; when they tried to detour around barriers, they were intercepted and hectored;

sentences.zh: 或有貨物，則抽分給賞，斷罪倍輸，倒囊而歸矣。

translations.literal: if they had goods, portions were withheld for rewards, convictions required double payment, and they returned with emptied bags.
translations.idiomatic: if they had goods, portions were seized as reward money, double fines imposed, and they went home with emptied purses.

sentences.zh: 聞者谘嗟，指為大小法場，與斯民相刃相靡刂，不啻仇敵，而其弊有不可勝言矣。

translations.literal: Hearers sighed with grief, calling them great and small execution grounds; with the people they clashed and wore each other down like enemies, and the abuses were beyond enumeration.
translations.idiomatic: Onlookers groaned, calling the stations great and small execution grounds; officials preyed on the people like enemies, and the abuses were beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 市易之設，本漢平準，將以製物之低昂而均通之。

translations.literal: The establishment of Market Purchase originated in Han's Equalization, intended to control goods' rise and fall and balance and circulate them.
translations.idiomatic: The Market Purchase system was modeled on the Han Equalization policy, intended to stabilize prices and keep commerce flowing.

sentences.zh: 其弊也，以官府作賈區，公取牙儈之利，而民不勝其煩矣。

translations.literal: Its abuse was that the government office became a trading quarter, publicly taking broker profits, and the people could not bear the vexation.
translations.idiomatic: Its abuse was that the government itself became a trading quarter, appropriating brokers' profits while the people could not bear the harassment.

sentences.zh: 熙寧三年，保平軍節度推官王韶倡為緣邊市易之說，丐假官錢為本。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xining, Wang Shao, military commissioner staff officer of Baoping Army, advocated frontier Market Purchase, begging to borrow official funds as capital.
translations.idiomatic: In 1070, Wang Shao, staff officer of the Baoping military commission, proposed frontier market purchase and asked to borrow government funds as capital.

sentences.zh: 詔秦鳳路經略司以川交子易物貨給之，因命韶為本路帥司幹當兼領市易事。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the Qinfeng circuit frontier commission to supply him goods in exchange for Sichuan jiaozi notes, and Wang Shao was appointed staff officer of the circuit command concurrently managing Market Purchase affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The Qinfeng frontier commission was ordered to supply goods in exchange for Sichuan paper notes, and Wang Shao was appointed to manage market purchase affairs for the circuit.

sentences.zh: 時欲移司於古渭城，李若愚等以為多聚貨以啟戎心，又妨秦州小馬、大馬私貿易，不可。

translations.literal: At the time they wished to move the office to Guwei city; Li Ruoyu and others held that amassing goods would arouse barbarian ambitions and also obstruct private trade in small and large horses at Qinzhou—this could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: When they proposed moving the office to Guwei, Li Ruoyu and others argued that stockpiling goods would provoke the tribes and disrupt private horse trade at Qinzhou—it should not be done.

sentences.zh: 文彥博、曾公亮、馮京皆韙之，韓絳亦以去秦州為非，唯王安石曰：「古渭置市易利害，臣雖不敢斷，然如若愚奏，必無可慮。」

translations.literal: Wen Yanbo, Zeng Gongliang, and Feng Jing all approved; Han Jiang also held leaving Qinzhou wrong; only Wang Anshi said: "The pros and cons of establishing Market Purchase at Guwei—I dare not decide, yet if it is as Li Ruoyu memorializes, there is surely nothing to worry about."
translations.idiomatic: Wen Yanbo, Zeng Gongliang, and Feng Jing all agreed; Han Jiang also opposed leaving Qinzhou; only Wang Anshi said, "I cannot judge the merits of market purchase at Guwei, but if Li Ruoyu is right, there is nothing to fear."

sentences.zh: 七月，詔轉運司詳度，復問陳升之。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, the transport commission was ordered to deliberate in detail, and Chen Shengzhi was again consulted.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month the transport commission was ordered to review the plan, and Chen Shengzhi was consulted again.

sentences.zh: 升之謂古渭極邊，恐啟群羌窺覬心。

translations.literal: Shengzhi said Guwei was at the extreme frontier and feared arousing the covetous hearts of the Qiang tribes.
translations.idiomatic: Shengzhi said Guwei lay at the extreme frontier and feared provoking Qiang ambitions.

sentences.zh: 安石乃言：「今蕃戶富者，往往蓄緡錢二二十萬，彼尚不畏劫奪，豈朝廷威靈，乃至衰弱如此？

translations.literal: Anshi then said: "Today wealthy barbarian households often store two or three hundred thousand strings of cash; they do not fear robbery—has court authority weakened to such a degree?
translations.idiomatic: Anshi replied: "Wealthy tribal households today often hoard two or three hundred thousand strings of cash without fear of robbery—has imperial authority truly weakened so far?

sentences.zh: 今欲連生羌，則形勢欲張，應接欲近。

translations.literal: Now wishing to link the raw Qiang, our posture must expand and our response must draw near.
translations.idiomatic: If we wish to win over the raw Qiang, we must extend our reach and draw our response closer.

sentences.zh: 古渭邊砦，便於應接，商旅並集，居者愈多，因建為軍，增兵馬，擇人守之，則形勢張矣。

translations.literal: Guwei's frontier stockade is convenient for response; merchants and travelers gather together, residents grow ever more numerous—thereby establish an army, increase troops and horses, choose men to guard it, and the posture expands.
translations.idiomatic: Guwei's frontier stockade is well placed for contact; as merchants gather and settlers increase, we can establish a garrison, add troops, and post capable commanders—thus extending our reach.

sentences.zh: 且蕃部得與官市，邊民無復逋負，足以懷來其心，因收其贏以助軍費，更辟荒土，異日可以聚兵。」

translations.literal: Moreover, when tribal departments can trade with the government, frontier people will no longer be in arrears, sufficient to win their hearts; thereby collect their profits to assist military expenses, further open wasteland—another day troops can be assembled."
translations.idiomatic: When tribes can trade with the government, frontier people will no longer be in debt, winning their loyalty; profits can fund the army and open new land for future garrisons."

sentences.zh: 時王安石為政，汲汲焉以財利兵革為先，其市易之說，已見於熙寧二年建議立均輸平準法之時，故王韶首迎合其意，而安石力主之，雖以李若愚、陳升之、韓絳諸人之議，而卒不可回。

translations.literal: At that time Wang Anshi held power, urgently putting finance and military reform first; his Market Purchase doctrine had already appeared when he proposed establishing Balanced Transport and Equalization in the second year of Xining; hence Wang Shao first catered to his intent, and Anshi strongly supported it—though Li Ruoyu, Chen Shengzhi, Han Jiang, and others objected, in the end it could not be turned back.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi was then in power, urgently prioritizing finance and military reform; his market purchase idea had appeared as early as his 1069 proposal for balanced transport and equalization. Wang Shao catered to his aims and Anshi strongly backed him; despite objections from Li Ruoyu, Chen Shengzhi, and Han Jiang, the policy could not be reversed.

sentences.zh: 五年，遂詔出內帑錢帛，置市易務於京師。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, an edict finally ordered disbursement of inner treasury cash and silks and establishment of a Market Purchase office in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In 1072, an edict ordered funds from the inner treasury and established a Market Purchase office in the capital.

sentences.zh: 先是，有魏繼宗者，自稱草澤，上言：「京師百貨無常價，貴賤相傾，富能奪，貧能與，乃可以為天下。

translations.literal: Earlier, one Wei Jizong, calling himself a man of the wilds, memorialized: "In the capital all goods have no fixed price; high and low overturn each other—only when the rich can seize and the poor can give can one govern the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, a man named Wei Jizong, calling himself a commoner, memorialized: "In the capital prices fluctuate wildly—the rich can corner markets and the poor can be aided; only then can the realm be governed.

sentences.zh: 今富人大姓，乘民之亟，牟利數倍，財既偏聚，國用亦屈。

translations.literal: Today great wealthy clans, seizing the people's urgency, profit several times over; wealth is already concentrated, and state revenues are also strained.
translations.idiomatic: Today wealthy clans exploit the people's distress for several-fold profit; wealth concentrates in their hands while state revenues suffer.

sentences.zh: 請假榷貨務錢，置常平市易司，擇通財之官任其責，求良賈為之轉易。

translations.literal: We request borrowing monopoly goods office funds, establishing an Ever-Normal Market Purchase bureau, selecting officials versed in finance to bear responsibility, and seeking good merchants to conduct exchanges.
translations.idiomatic: I ask to borrow funds from the monopoly goods office, establish an Ever-Normal Market Purchase bureau, appoint capable financial officials, and employ reliable merchants to trade.

sentences.zh: 使審知市物之價，賤則增價市之，貴則損價鬻之，因收餘息，以給公上。」

translations.literal: Let them carefully know market goods' prices: when cheap, raise price and buy; when dear, lower price and sell; thereby collect surplus interest to supply the public treasury."
translations.idiomatic: They should track market prices, buying when prices are low and selling when high, collecting surplus profit for the treasury."

sentences.zh: 於是中書奏在京置市易務官。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Secretariat memorialized to establish Market Purchase officials in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat then proposed establishing Market Purchase officials in the capital.

sentences.zh: 凡貨之可市及滯於民而不售者，平其價市之，願以易官物者聽。

translations.literal: All marketable goods and those stagnating among the people unsold—the government was to set fair price and buy them; those wishing to exchange for government goods were permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Marketable goods and those unsold among the people were to be bought at fair prices; those wishing to exchange for government goods were permitted.

sentences.zh: 若欲市於官，則度其抵而貸之錢，責期使償，半歲輸息十一，及歲倍之。

translations.literal: If they wished to buy from the government, their collateral was assessed and money lent; repayment was required by deadline—half-year interest one in eleven, full year doubled.
translations.idiomatic: Merchants wishing to buy from the government received loans against collateral, due within a set term—interest of one part in eleven per half year, doubled for a full year.

sentences.zh: 凡諸司配率，並仰給焉。

translations.literal: All agencies' apportioned levies were to rely on it for supply.
translations.idiomatic: All agencies' apportioned requisitions were to be supplied from it.

sentences.zh: 以呂嘉問為提舉，賜內庫錢百萬緡、京東路錢八十七萬緡為本。

translations.literal: Lü Jiawen was made commissioner; one million strings from the inner treasury and 870,000 strings from Jingdong circuit were granted as capital.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Jiawen was appointed commissioner, with one million strings from the inner treasury and 870,000 from Jingdong as capital.

sentences.zh: 三司請立市易條，有「兼並之家，較固取利，有害新法，本務覺察，三司按治」之文，帝削去之。

translations.literal: The Three Departments requested establishing Market Purchase regulations with language that "monopolizing households, obstinately taking profit, harming the new law—the office shall detect and the Three Departments investigate"; the emperor struck it out.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Departments proposed regulations including prosecution of monopolists who obstructed the new law; the emperor deleted that clause.

sentences.zh: 七月，以榷貨務為市易西務下界，市易務為東務上界，以在京商稅院、雜買務、雜賣場隸焉。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, the Monopoly Goods Office became the Market Purchase western lower division, the Market Purchase office the eastern upper division; the capital commercial tax office, miscellaneous purchase office, and miscellaneous sales yard were placed under it.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month the Monopoly Goods Office became the western lower division of Market Purchase and the Market Purchase office the eastern upper division; the capital commercial tax office and miscellaneous purchase and sales yards were placed under it.

sentences.zh: 又賜錢帛五十萬，於鎮洮軍置司。

translations.literal: Another 500,000 in cash and silks was granted to establish an office at Zhentao Army.
translations.idiomatic: Another 500,000 in cash and silks was granted to establish an office at Zhentao Army.

sentences.zh: 市易極苛細，道路怨謗者籍籍。

translations.literal: Market Purchase was extremely minute in regulation; complaints along the roads were abundant.
translations.idiomatic: Market Purchase regulations were extremely petty, and complaints along the roads were widespread.

sentences.zh: 上以諭安石，請宣示事實，帝以鬻冰、市梳樸等數事語之，安石皆辯解。

translations.literal: The emperor informed Anshi and asked him to proclaim the facts; the emperor cited selling ice, marketing combs, and several other matters; Anshi defended them all.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told Anshi to clarify the facts, citing sales of ice and combs among other complaints; Anshi defended them all.

sentences.zh: 後帝復言：「市易鬻果太煩碎，罷之如何？」

translations.literal: Later the emperor again said: "Market Purchase selling fruit is too trivial—how about abolishing it?"
translations.idiomatic: Later the emperor said again, "Market Purchase in fruit is too trivial—should we abolish it?"

sentences.zh: 安石謂：「立法當論有害於人與否，不當以煩碎廢也。」

translations.literal: Anshi said: "When legislating one should discuss whether it harms people, not abolish because of triviality."
translations.idiomatic: Anshi replied, "Legislation should be judged by whether it harms people, not abolished for being trivial."

sentences.zh: 自是諸州上供藨席、黃蘆之類六十色，悉令計直，從民願鬻者市之以給用。

translations.literal: From this time, sixty types of tribute items from various prefectures such as rush mats and yellow reeds were all ordered priced; those the people wished to sell were bought for use.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter sixty types of tribute goods such as rush mats and yellow reeds from the prefectures were priced and bought from willing sellers for official use.

sentences.zh: 六年，詔在京市易幹當公事孫迪同兩浙、淮東轉運司，議置杭州市易務利病以聞。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, an edict ordered capital Market Purchase staff officer Sun Di together with the two Zhe and Huaidong transport commissions to discuss establishing Hangzhou Market Purchase and report benefits and harms.
translations.idiomatic: In 1073, Sun Di of the capital Market Purchase office was ordered with the two Zhe and Huaidong transport commissions to report on establishing Market Purchase at Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 其後以市易上界所償內帑錢二十萬緡假之為本。

translations.literal: Afterward 200,000 strings repaid to the inner treasury by the Market Purchase upper division were lent as capital.
translations.idiomatic: Later 200,000 strings repaid to the inner treasury by the upper division were lent as capital.

sentences.zh: 又賜夔州路轉運司度僧牒五百，置市易於黔州，選本路在任已替官監之，仍以知州或通判提舉。

translations.literal: Another 500 monk certificates were granted to the Kuizhou transport commission; Market Purchase was established at Qian prefecture, selecting current and former circuit officials to supervise, with prefect or vice-prefect as commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Five hundred monk certificates were granted to the Kuizhou transport commission; Market Purchase was established at Qianzhou, supervised by circuit officials past and present under the prefect or vice-prefect.

sentences.zh: 令在京市易務及開封府司錄同詳度諸行利病，於是詳定所請：「約諸行利入薄厚，輸免行錢以祿吏，蠲其供官之物。

translations.literal: The capital Market Purchase office and Kaifeng prefecture registrar were ordered jointly to deliberate trade guild benefits and harms; the detailed proposal requested: "Estimate guilds' profits thick and thin, collect exemption fees to pay clerks, and remit their goods supplied to government.
translations.idiomatic: The capital Market Purchase office and Kaifeng registrar were ordered to review guild practices; their proposal: "Assess guild profits, collect exemption fees to pay clerks, and remit goods supplied to government.

sentences.zh: 禁中所須，並下雜賣場、雜買務。

translations.literal: Palace requirements were all sent down to the miscellaneous sales yard and miscellaneous purchase office.
translations.idiomatic: Palace requisitions were all routed through the miscellaneous sales and purchase offices.

sentences.zh: 置市司估物價低昂，凡內外官司欲占物價，悉於是乎取決。」

translations.literal: A market office was established to assess goods' prices high and low; all inner and outer agencies wishing to fix on prices were entirely to decide there."
translations.idiomatic: A market office was established to assess prices; all government agencies seeking price references were to rely on it."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: Approval was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved.

sentences.zh: 改提舉在京市易務為都提舉市易司，諸州市易務皆隸焉。

translations.literal: The commissioner of capital Market Purchase was changed to Director of the Market Purchase Bureau; Market Purchase offices in all prefectures were placed under it.
translations.idiomatic: The capital Market Purchase commissioner was renamed Director of the Market Purchase Bureau, with all prefectural offices subordinate to it.

sentences.zh: 又詔三司幹當公事李杞等同詳度成都置市易務。

translations.literal: Another edict ordered Three Departments staff officer Li Qi and others jointly to deliberate establishing Market Purchase at Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Li Qi of the Three Departments was also ordered to review establishing Market Purchase at Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 七年，帝與輔臣論及成都市易事。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, the emperor discussed Chengdu Market Purchase affairs with chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: In 1074 the emperor discussed Chengdu Market Purchase with his chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 馮京曰：「曩因榷市物，致王小波之亂，今頗以市易為言。」

translations.literal: Feng Jing said: "Formerly because of monopolizing market goods, Wang Xiaobo's rebellion was caused; today there is much talk about Market Purchase."
translations.idiomatic: Feng Jing said, "Monopolizing market goods once caused Wang Xiaobo's rebellion; today there is much complaint about Market Purchase."

sentences.zh: 安石曰：「彼以饑民眾，官不之恤，相聚為盜耳。」

translations.literal: Anshi said: "That was because famine victims were numerous and officials did not relieve them—they gathered as bandits, that is all."
translations.idiomatic: Anshi replied, "That was because famine victims were numerous and officials failed to relieve them—they banded together as robbers, nothing more."

sentences.zh: 帝問：「李杞行邪？」

translations.literal: The emperor asked: "Has Li Qi gone?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, "Has Li Qi departed?"

sentences.zh: 安石曰：「未也。

translations.literal: Anshi said: "Not yet.
translations.idiomatic: Anshi said, "Not yet.

sentences.zh: 然保市易必不能致亂。」

translations.literal: Yet I guarantee Market Purchase certainly cannot cause disorder."
translations.idiomatic: But I guarantee Market Purchase cannot cause disorder."

sentences.zh: 帝猶慮蜀人駭擾，安石謂：「已遣使乃遽罷，豈不為四方笑？」

translations.literal: The emperor still feared Sichuan people would be alarmed and disturbed; Anshi said: "An envoy has already been sent—if we suddenly stop, will we not be laughed at by the four directions?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor still feared alarming the people of Shu; Anshi said, "We have already sent an envoy—if we stop now, will we not be mocked throughout the realm?"

sentences.zh: 乃已。

translations.literal: And so it stopped there.
translations.idiomatic: And the matter rested there.

sentences.zh: 然其後竟罷杞等詳度。

translations.literal: Yet afterward Qi and the others' deliberation was finally abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Yet afterward Li Qi and his colleagues' review was finally cancelled.

sentences.zh: 三月，詔權三司使曾布、翰林學士呂惠卿同究詰市易事。

translations.literal: In the third month, an edict ordered acting Three Departments commissioner Zeng Bu and Hanlin academician Lü Huiqing jointly to investigate Market Purchase affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Zeng Bu, acting Three Departments commissioner, and Hanlin academician Lü Huiqing were ordered jointly to investigate Market Purchase.

sentences.zh: 先是，帝出手詔付布，謂市易司市物，頗害小民之業，眾言喧嘩。

translations.literal: Earlier, the emperor handed Bu a personal edict saying the Market Purchase office's buying of goods considerably harmed common people's livelihoods, and public clamor was loud.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the emperor had handed Bu a personal edict saying Market Purchase harmed common people's livelihoods and provoked widespread outcry.

sentences.zh: 布乃引監市易務魏繼宗之言，以為呂嘉問多取息以幹賞，商旅所有者盡收，市肆所無者必索，率賤市貴鬻，廣裒贏餘，是挾官府為兼並也。

translations.literal: Bu then cited Market Purchase supervisor Wei Jizong's words, holding that Lü Jiawen took much interest to seek rewards; whatever merchants and travelers owned was all taken in, what market stalls lacked was always demanded; generally buying cheap and selling dear, broadly amassing surplus—this was wielding government office for monopoly.
translations.idiomatic: Bu cited supervisor Wei Jizong, charging that Lü Jiawen inflated interest to win rewards, seized all merchants possessed, demanded what shops lacked, bought cheap and sold dear, and amassed profits—using government power to monopolize trade.

sentences.zh: 王安石具奏，明其不然。

translations.literal: Wang Anshi submitted a full memorial clarifying it was not so.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi submitted a full rebuttal.

sentences.zh: 乃更令惠卿偕布究詰之。

translations.literal: Thereupon Huiqing was again ordered to join Bu in investigation.
translations.idiomatic: Huiqing was then ordered to join Bu in the investigation.

sentences.zh: 帝尋復以手劄賜布，令求對，布即上行人所訴，並疏惠卿奸欺狀，且言：「臣自立朝以來，每聞德音，未嘗不欲以王道治天下，今市易之為虐，凜凜乎間架、除陌之事矣。

translations.literal: The emperor soon again bestowed a personal note on Bu, ordering him to request audience; Bu immediately submitted merchants' complaints and also detailed Huiqing's deceitful conduct, saying: "Since I entered court, whenever I heard virtuous pronouncements I always wished to govern the realm by the kingly way; today Market Purchase's cruelty is as chilling as the jianjia and chumo affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor soon sent Bu another personal note ordering an audience; Bu submitted merchants' complaints and detailed Huiqing's deceit, saying, "Since entering court I have always wished to govern by the kingly way; today Market Purchase's cruelty rivals the Tang jianjia and chumo exactions.

sentences.zh: 嘉問奏：『近遣官往湖南販茶，陝西販鹽，兩浙販紗，皆未敢計息。』

translations.literal: Jiawen memorialized: 'Recently officials were sent to Hunan to sell tea, Shaanxi to sell salt, the two Zhe to sell yarn—all did not dare calculate interest.'
translations.idiomatic: Jiawen reported, 'Officials were recently sent to sell tea in Hunan, salt in Shaanxi, and yarn in the two Zhe circuits—none dared yet calculate interest.'

sentences.zh: 臣以謂如此政事，書之簡牘，不獨唐、虞、三代所無，曆觀秦、漢以來衰亂之世，恐未之有也。」

translations.literal: Your subject considers that such governance, written on bamboo slips—not only absent in Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties—surveying Qin, Han, and later ages of decline and disorder, I fear has never existed."
translations.idiomatic: Such governance, I believe, is unknown not only in the age of Yao and Shun but in every decadent age since Qin and Han."

sentences.zh: 四月，布復陳薛向罪茶儈不當，帝惻然谘嗟；

translations.literal: In the fourth month, Bu again stated Xue Xiang's punishing tea brokers was improper; the emperor was moved and sighed with sympathy;
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Bu again argued that Xue Xiang had wrongly punished tea brokers; the emperor sighed in sympathy;

sentences.zh: 及言三司決責商人多濫，時帝猶必欲按治。

translations.literal: and spoke of the Three Departments' judgments and punishments of merchants being mostly excessive; at the time the emperor still insisted on investigation and punishment.
translations.idiomatic: and said the Three Departments' punishments of merchants were mostly excessive; yet the emperor still insisted on proceeding.

sentences.zh: 而安石主用惠卿不可去，蓋謀變其事也。

translations.literal: Yet Anshi insisted on employing Huiqing and that he could not be removed—likely plotting to change the matter.
translations.idiomatic: But Anshi insisted Huiqing must stay—likely plotting to change the outcome.

sentences.zh: 帝疑焉，故仍以屬布。

translations.literal: The emperor was doubtful, and therefore still assigned it to Bu.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was doubtful and therefore kept the matter with Bu.

sentences.zh: 既而中書奏事已，帝論及市易，且曰：「朝廷設此，本欲為平準之法以便民，今正爾相反，使中下之民失業若此，宜修補其法。」

translations.literal: Shortly afterward, when the Secretariat finished reporting business, the emperor discussed Market Purchase and said: "The court established this originally intending the Equalization method to benefit the people; now it is exactly the opposite, causing middle and lower people to lose livelihoods like this—the law should be repaired."
translations.idiomatic: When the Secretariat finished its report, the emperor discussed Market Purchase and said, "We established this to benefit the people through equalization; now it does the opposite, driving middle and lower classes from their livelihoods—the law must be amended."

sentences.zh: 令元詳定呂嘉問、吳安持同韓維、孫永問行人輸錢免行利病。

translations.literal: He ordered detailed deliberation by Lü Jiawen and Wu Anchi together with Han Wei and Sun Yong on merchants paying money to exempt transit duties—benefits and harms.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Lü Jiawen and Wu Anchi with Han Wei and Sun Yong to review merchants' payment of transit exemption fees.

sentences.zh: 參知政事馮京曰：「開封祥符縣給民錢，有出息抵當銀絹米麥、緩急喪葬之目七八種。

translations.literal: Vice Grand Councillor Feng Jing said: "Kaifeng Xiangfu county gives the people money with seven or eight categories bearing interest and collateral in silver, silk, rice, wheat, urgent and funeral needs.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Grand Councillor Feng Jing said, "Kaifeng's Xiangfu county lends money to the people in seven or eight categories—with interest, collateral in silver, silk, grain, and provisions for emergencies and funerals.

sentences.zh: 其初給錢，往往願請，積數既多，實艱輸送。」

translations.literal: At first when money was given, people often wished to request it; once numbers accumulated, repayment was truly difficult."
translations.idiomatic: At first people eagerly borrowed; once debts accumulated, repayment became truly difficult."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「如此，吾民安得泰然也？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Like this, how can our people be at ease?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "How can our people live in peace like this?"

sentences.zh: 時布與惠卿方究市易事，率數日一對。

translations.literal: At that time Bu and Huiqing were investigating Market Purchase affairs, generally meeting the emperor every few days.
translations.idiomatic: Bu and Huiqing were then investigating Market Purchase, meeting the emperor every few days.

sentences.zh: 帝初是布言，已而從惠卿之請，拘魏繼宗於開封府。

translations.literal: The emperor at first agreed with Bu's words; afterward following Huiqing's request, Wei Jizong was detained at the Kaifeng prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor at first sided with Bu; then, at Huiqing's request, detained Wei Jizong at Kaifeng prefecture.

sentences.zh: 既而布與惠卿即東府再詰行人，所訴狀如前不變。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward Bu and Huiqing at the Eastern Hall again questioned merchants; their complaints remained as before, unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Bu and Huiqing then questioned merchants again at the Eastern Hall; their complaints were unchanged.

sentences.zh: 而安石懇求去位，引惠卿執政。

translations.literal: Yet Anshi earnestly requested to leave office and brought Huiqing into government.
translations.idiomatic: Anshi then earnestly requested to leave office and brought Huiqing into power.

sentences.zh: 提舉楚州市易蔣之奇奏：「監務王景彰榷市商人物非法，及虛作中糴入務，立詭名糴之，白輸息錢，謂之『幹息』；

translations.literal: Chuzhou Market Purchase commissioner Jiang Zhiqi memorialized: "Supervisor Wang Jingzhang illegally monopolized merchants' goods in the market, and falsely made central purchases entering the office, establishing deceptive names to buy them, paying interest money in white, called 'dry interest';
translations.idiomatic: Chuzhou Market Purchase commissioner Jiang Zhiqi reported: "Supervisor Wang Jingzhang illegally seized merchants' goods, fabricated central purchases, used false names to buy grain, and paid interest under the table as 'dry interest';

sentences.zh: 又抑賈販毋得至他郡，多為留難。」

translations.literal: he also suppressed merchants from reaching other prefectures, often creating delays and difficulties."
translations.idiomatic: he also blocked merchants from reaching other prefectures and created many obstructions."

sentences.zh: 帝謂輔臣曰：「景彰違法害人，宜即治其罪。」

translations.literal: The emperor told chief ministers: "Jingzhang violated the law and harmed people—his crime should be immediately punished."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told his ministers, "Jingzhang broke the law and harmed people—he should be punished at once."

sentences.zh: 時呂惠卿已參朝政，而究詰市易未竟，詔促之，惠卿請令中書悉取桉牘異同以奏。

translations.literal: At that time Lü Huiqing had already joined court governance, yet Market Purchase investigation was not finished; an edict urged completion; Huiqing requested the Secretariat gather all case records' discrepancies and report.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Huiqing had already joined the government, but the Market Purchase investigation was unfinished; when urged to complete it, Huiqing asked the Secretariat to gather all case records and report discrepancies.

sentences.zh: 後二日，布對延和殿，條祈先後所陳，並較治平、熙寧出入錢物數以聞。

translations.literal: Two days later Bu answered at Yanhe Hall, itemizing what he had stated before and after, and comparing Zhiping and Xining revenue and expenditure figures to report.
translations.idiomatic: Two days later Bu reported at Yanhe Hall, summarizing his prior statements and comparing Zhiping and Xining revenue figures.

sentences.zh: 帝方慮歲費浸廣，令布送中書。

translations.literal: The emperor was then concerned annual expenses were gradually expanding and ordered Bu to send it to the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, concerned that annual expenses were growing, ordered Bu to send his report to the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 五月，乃詔章惇、曾孝寬即軍器監鞫布所究市易事，又令戶房會財賦數，與布所陳異；

translations.literal: In the fifth month, an edict ordered Zhang Dun and Zeng Xiaokuan at the Armaments Directorate to interrogate Bu's Market Purchase investigation; the accounts office was also ordered to tally revenue figures, which differed from Bu's statements;
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Zhang Dun and Zeng Xiaokuan at the Armaments Directorate were ordered to interrogate Bu's investigation; the accounts office tallied revenues that differed from Bu's figures;

sentences.zh: 而呂嘉問亦以雜買務多入月息不覺，皆從公坐有差。

translations.literal: Lü Jiawen also, because the miscellaneous purchase office took in much monthly interest unnoticed, all received differentiated punishment for collective fault.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Jiawen was also punished because the miscellaneous purchase office had accepted unrecorded monthly interest—all received differentiated penalties for collective fault.

sentences.zh: 未幾，布褫職，與嘉問俱出守郡，魏繼宗仍奪秩勒停。

translations.literal: Before long, Bu was stripped of office; he and Jiawen were both sent out to guard prefectures; Wei Jizong still had rank removed and was ordered to cease service.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Bu was dismissed and sent to a prefecture, as was Jiawen; Wei Jizong was stripped of rank and suspended.

sentences.zh: 初，市易之建，布實預之。

translations.literal: At first, when Market Purchase was established, Bu had actually participated in it.
translations.idiomatic: Bu had actually helped establish Market Purchase in the first place.

sentences.zh: 後揣上意有疑，遂急治嘉問，而惠卿與布有夙怨，故卒擠之，而市易如故。

translations.literal: Later sensing the emperor's doubts, he hurriedly prosecuted Jiawen; Huiqing and Bu had an old grudge, so in the end he was squeezed out, while Market Purchase remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: Later sensing the emperor's doubts, he hurriedly prosecuted Jiawen; Huiqing's old grudge against Bu ensured his downfall, while Market Purchase continued unchanged.

sentences.zh: 三司使章惇請假內藏錢五百萬緡，令市易司有幹局者，分四路入中，計見鹽引及乘賤糴買。

translations.literal: Three Departments commissioner Zhang Dun requested borrowing five million strings from the inner treasury, ordering Market Purchase staff with initiative to enter bids on four routes, calculating visible salt certificates and buying when prices were low.
translations.idiomatic: Three Departments commissioner Zhang Dun asked to borrow five million strings from the inner treasury for Market Purchase agents to bid on four routes, buying salt certificates and grain when prices were low.

sentences.zh: 詔假二百萬緡。

translations.literal: An edict lent two million strings.
translations.idiomatic: Two million strings were lent by edict.

sentences.zh: 八年，復呂嘉問提舉市易。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, Lü Jiawen was restored as Market Purchase commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In 1075 Lü Jiawen was restored as Market Purchase commissioner.

sentences.zh: 二月，鳳翔、大名、真定府、永興、安肅軍，秦、瀛、定、越、真州，並置市易司。

translations.literal: In the second month, Fengxiang, Daming, Zhending prefectures, Yongxing, Ansujun, Qin, Ying, Ding, Yue, and Zhen prefectures all established Market Purchase bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Market Purchase bureaus were established at Fengxiang, Daming, Zhending, Yongxing, Ansujun, and the prefectures of Qin, Ying, Ding, Yue, and Zhen.

sentences.zh: 以惠州阜民監錢十萬緡給廣州市易務，司農寺坊場錢三十萬緡給鄆州市易。

translations.literal: 100,000 strings from Huizhou Fumin prison were given to Guangzhou Market Purchase; 300,000 strings from the Ministry of Agriculture temple estate were given to Yunzhou Market Purchase.
translations.idiomatic: 100,000 strings from Huizhou's Fumin prison funded Guangzhou Market Purchase; 300,000 from the Ministry of Agriculture funded Yunzhou Market Purchase.

sentences.zh: 九年，又以在京市易司物貨十五萬緡給熙河市易司。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, another 150,000 strings in goods from the capital Market Purchase bureau were given to the Xihe Market Purchase bureau.
translations.idiomatic: In 1076 another 150,000 strings in goods from the capital Market Purchase bureau were sent to the Xihe bureau.

sentences.zh: 九月，中書言：「市易息錢並市例錢，總收百三十三萬二千緡有奇。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, the Secretariat said: "Market Purchase interest monies together with market-rate monies totaled receipt of 1,332,000-odd strings.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the Secretariat reported: "Market Purchase interest and market-rate revenues totaled more than 1,332,000 strings.

sentences.zh: 詔嘉問、安持等推恩有差。

translations.literal: An edict granted differentiated favor rewards to Jiawen, Anchi, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Jiawen, Anchi, and others received differentiated imperial rewards by edict.

sentences.zh: 自後凡二年一較。

translations.literal: From thereafter, every two years there was one comparison.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, accounts were reconciled every two years.

sentences.zh: 十年，定上界本錢以七百萬緡為額，不足，以歲所收息益之；

translations.literal: In the tenth year, the upper circuit's principal capital was fixed at a quota of seven million strings; if insufficient, it was supplemented by interest collected that year;
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year (1077), the capital for the upper circuit was capped at seven million strings of cash, with any shortfall made up from annual interest receipts.

sentences.zh: 其貸內帑錢，歲償以息二十萬緡。

translations.literal: For those who borrowed inner treasury money, yearly repayment was twenty thousand strings from interest.
translations.idiomatic: Loans from the inner treasury were repaid at twenty thousand strings per year from interest earnings.

sentences.zh: 元豐元年，以都提舉王居卿請，令貸市易錢貨者，許用金帛等為抵，收息毋過一分二厘，不及年者月計之，願皆得錢或欲以物貨兼給者聽。

translations.literal: Yuanfeng year 1, following chief superintendent Wang Juqing's request, those borrowing Market Purchase funds were permitted to use gold, silks, and the like as collateral; interest collected must not exceed 1.2 fen per unit; for periods less than a year, monthly calculation; those wishing all cash or wishing combined goods-and-cash payment were permitted.
translations.idiomatic: In 1078, at the request of chief superintendent Wang Juqing, borrowers of Market Purchase capital were allowed to pledge gold, silk, and similar goods as collateral. Interest was capped at twelve per thousand per annum, calculated monthly for loans under a year; applicants could take the full amount in cash or accept a mixed payment in cash and goods.

sentences.zh: 市易司請遣官以物貨至諸路貿易，十萬緡以上期以二年，二十萬緡以上三年，斂及三分者比遞年推恩，八分者理為任，期盡不及者勿賞，官吏廩給並罷。

translations.literal: The Market Purchase Bureau requested dispatching officials with goods to various circuits to trade; 100,000 strings or more: two-year term; 200,000 or more: three years; those collecting three fen received rewards compared by year of seniority, eight fen counted as merit term, at term end if not reached no reward, officials' salary provisions all abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The Market Purchase Bureau proposed sending officials to trade state goods in the circuits: tours of one hundred thousand strings or more had a two-year deadline, two hundred thousand or more had three years. Officials who returned thirty percent profit received preferment by year of seniority; eighty percent counted toward tenure qualification. Those who missed their targets received no reward, and official salaries and allowances on such tours were withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 二年，經制熙河路邊防財用李憲言：蕃賈與牙儈私市，其貨皆由他路避稅入秦州。

translations.literal: Year 2, commissioner for Xijing Circuit frontier finances Li Xian said: Fan merchants with brokers privately traded; their goods all by other routes evaded tax entering Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In 1079, Li Xian, commissioner for Xijing frontier finances, reported that Tibetan merchants and their brokers were dealing privately, routing goods through other roads to evade taxes before they reached Qinzhou.
