sentences.zh: 乃令秦熙河岷州、通遠軍五市易務，募牙儈引蕃貨赴市易務中賈，私市者許糾告，賞倍所告之數。

translations.literal: Thereupon ordered five Market Purchase bureaus at Qin, Xihe, Minzhou, and Tongyuan Army; recruited brokers to lead Fan goods to Market Purchase bureaus for middle pricing; private traders permitted to inform, reward double the reported amount.
translations.idiomatic: The court then set up five Market Purchase offices in Qinzhou, Xihe, Minzhou, and Tongyuan—recruiting brokers to channel Tibetan goods into official markets at regulated prices—and allowed informants against private trade, paying rewards of double the amount reported.

sentences.zh: 以田宅抵市易錢久不償者，估實直，如賣坊場、河渡法；

translations.literal: Those using fields and houses to pledge Market Purchase money long unpaid—assess true value, as the law for selling workshops and ferry crossings;
translations.idiomatic: For debtors who had pledged homes and land for Market Purchase loans and fallen long in arrears, property was appraised at true value and sold under the same rules used for workshops and ferry concessions.

sentences.zh: 若未輸錢者，官收其租息，在京市易務亦如之。

translations.literal: If money not yet paid in, the government collected its rent and interest; the capital Market Purchase bureau likewise.
translations.idiomatic: When the principal had not yet been repaid, the state collected rent and interest on the property; the capital Market Purchase office followed the same practice.

sentences.zh: 三年，詔免行月納錢不及百者皆免，凡除八千六百五十四人。

translations.literal: Year 3, an edict exempted those whose monthly Exemption fee payment was less than one hundred—all exempted, in total removing 8,654 persons.
translations.idiomatic: In 1080, an edict exempted all Exemption-fee payers whose monthly installment fell below a hundred cash—8,654 people in all were relieved.

sentences.zh: 九月，王居卿又言：「市易法有三：結保貸請，一也；

translations.literal: Ninth month, Wang Juqing again said: "Market Purchase law has three: association-guarantee loans, one;
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, Wang Juqing again memorialized: "The Market Purchase system has three parts: mutual-guarantee lending is the first;

sentences.zh: 契要金銀為抵，二也；

translations.literal: contracts with gold and silver as pledge, two;
translations.idiomatic: pledged loans secured by gold and silver contracts are the second;

sentences.zh: 貿遷物貨，三也。

translations.literal: transporting-trading goods, three.
translations.idiomatic: and government trading and transshipment of goods is the third.

sentences.zh: 三者惟保貸法行之久，負失益多，往歲罷貸錢而物貨如故。

translations.literal: Of the three, only guarantee-loan law had been practiced long, losses owed increasingly many, in past years lending was abolished yet goods trade as before.
translations.idiomatic: Of the three, only the guarantee-lending program had run longest and bad debt had kept mounting. Lending had been suspended the year before, yet goods trading continued unchanged.

sentences.zh: 請自今所貸歲約毋過二百萬緡，聽舊戶貸請以相濟續，非舊戶惟用抵當、貿遷之法。」

translations.literal: Request from now annual loans approx. not exceed 2 million strings; permit old accounts to borrow to mutually support continuation, non-old accounts only use pawn, transporting-trade methods."
translations.idiomatic: He asked that annual lending be capped at about two million strings, that established customers alone receive loans to keep the pool revolving, and that new customers be limited to collateral loans and official trade.

sentences.zh: 詔中書立法以聞。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the Secretariat to legislate and report.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the Secretariat to draft regulations and report back.

sentences.zh: 於是中書奏：「在京物貨，許舊戶貸請，斂而復散，通所負毋過三百萬緡，諸路毋過四之一。」

translations.literal: Thereupon the Secretariat memorialized: "In capital goods, permit old accounts to borrow, gather and re-disperse, total owed not exceed 3 million strings, circuits not exceed one-fourth."
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat then proposed: in the capital, established merchants might borrow under the gather-and-release system, with total outstanding debt capped at three million strings; in the circuits, at one-fourth of that amount.

sentences.zh: 詔如所奏。

translations.literal: An edict as memorialized.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved as proposed.

sentences.zh: 是歲，經制熙河邊防財用司會其置司以來所收息：元豐初四十一萬四千六百二十六緡、石，次年六十八萬四千九十九緡、石。

translations.literal: This year, the Xijing frontier finances bureau tallied interest received since establishing the bureau: Yuanfeng start 414,626 strings/shi, next year 684,099 strings/shi.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Xijing frontier finances office totaled interest since its founding: 414,626 strings and shi in early Yuanfeng, 684,099 the following year.

sentences.zh: 四年，從都提舉賈青請，於新舊城外內置四抵當所，遣官掌之，罷市易上界等處抵當以便民。

translations.literal: Year 4, following chief superintendent Jia Qing's request, inside and outside new and old city walls set up four pawn offices, dispatched officials to administer, abolished Market Purchase upper circuit etc. pawn to benefit people.
translations.idiomatic: In 1081, following Jia Qing's proposal, four pawn offices were established inside and outside the inner and outer city walls under appointed managers, replacing the inconvenient pawn counters attached to the upper Market Purchase circuit.

sentences.zh: 五年，詔外內市易務所負錢，寬以三歲，均月限以輸，限內罰息並除之。

translations.literal: Year 5, an edict: inner and outer Market Purchase bureaus' owed money, extended to three years, averaged monthly limits to pay in, within term penalty interest all exempted.
translations.idiomatic: In 1082, an edict gave inner and outer Market Purchase debtors three years to repay in equal monthly installments and canceled all penalty interest due within that period.

sentences.zh: 先是，王安禮在開封日，有負市易錢者，累訴於庭。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Wang Anli was in Kaifeng, those owing Market Purchase money repeatedly sued at court.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while Wang Anli served in Kaifeng, debtors of Market Purchase loans had repeatedly brought suit in his court.

sentences.zh: 安禮既執政，言於帝曰：「市易法行，取息滋多，而輸官不時者有罰息，民至窮困。

translations.literal: Anli having taken power, said to emperor: "Market Purchase law runs, interest taken increasingly much, yet those paying to government not on time have penalty interest, people to extreme poverty.
translations.idiomatic: Once in office, Wang Anli told the emperor, "Under the Market Purchase system interest revenue keeps rising, but borrowers who miss payment deadlines face penalty interest until the common people are driven to destitution.

sentences.zh: 願詔蠲之。」

translations.literal: Wish edict to remit it."
translations.idiomatic: I beg that Your Majesty issue an edict remitting these penalties."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「群臣未有為朕言者，其令民以限輸，免其罰息。」

translations.literal: Emperor said: "Ministers have not spoken for Us on this, let people pay within limits, exempt their penalty interest.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied, "No minister has raised this with me before. Let the people repay on schedule and forgive their penalty interest."

sentences.zh: 安禮退，批詔加「內外」字。

translations.literal: Anli withdrew, annotated edict adding "inner and outer" characters.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Anli withdrew, he annotated the draft edict to add the words "throughout the realm."

sentences.zh: 蔡確曰：「方帝有旨，無外內字，公欲增詔邪？」

translations.literal: Cai Que said: "Just now emperor had order, no outer-inner character, sir wish to augment edict?"
translations.idiomatic: Cai Que objected: "The emperor's command made no distinction between capital and provinces. Do you mean to broaden the edict?"

sentences.zh: 安禮曰：「亦不止言內字。」

translations.literal: Anli said: "Also not only speaking inner character."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anli answered, "I am not adding only 'inner' either."

sentences.zh: 卒加之。

translations.literal: In the end added it.
translations.idiomatic: The wording was added in the end.

sentences.zh: 八月，置饒州景德鎮瓷窯博易務。

translations.literal: Eighth month, established Raozhou Jingdezhen porcelain kiln Boyi bureau.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, a state trading office for porcelain kilns was established at Jingdezhen in Raozhou.

sentences.zh: 六年，蘭州增置市易務，以通蕃漢貿易。

translations.literal: Year 6, Lanzhou added Market Purchase bureau, to connect Fan and Han trade.
translations.idiomatic: In 1083, Lanzhou gained an additional Market Purchase office to promote trade between Tibetans and Han Chinese.

sentences.zh: 七年，改市易下界為榷貨務。

translations.literal: Year 7, changed Market Purchase lower circuit to Monopoly Goods bureau.
translations.idiomatic: In 1084, the lower Market Purchase circuit was renamed the Monopoly Goods Bureau.

sentences.zh: 令諸州旬估物價既定，報提舉司，提舉司下所部州，州下所屬，募民出抵或錢以市，收息毋過二分。

translations.literal: Ordered various prefectures: every ten days estimate prices fixed, report to supervisory commission, commission down to subordinate prefectures, prefectures down to subordinates, recruit people to offer pledge or money to market, interest collect not exceed two fen.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectures were to set prices every ten days, report through the supervisory commission to subordinate counties, and recruit merchants to trade with collateral or cash—interest capped at twenty per thousand.

sentences.zh: 詔諸路常平司錢留其半，以二分為市易抵當。

translations.literal: An edict: each circuit Ever-Normal granary funds keep half, use two fen for Market Purchase pawn.
translations.idiomatic: An edict required each circuit to keep half its Ever-Normal treasury funds and allocate twenty percent for Market Purchase pawn offices.

sentences.zh: 蓋自五年賈青以平準物價與金銀之類，行抵當於畿縣，次年行之諸路，以常平、市易賒貸及寬剩錢為本，五路各十萬緡，餘路五萬緡。

translations.literal: Essentially from year 5 Jia Qing with stabilizing prices and gold-silver types, ran pawn in capital counties, next year ran in circuits, using Ever-Normal, Market Purchase credit and surplus money as capital, five circuits each 100,000 strings, other circuits 50,000.
translations.idiomatic: Since 1082 Jia Qing had used price stabilization and gold and silver collateral to run pawn offices in the metropolitan counties, extending the practice to the circuits the next year with capital from Ever-Normal funds, Market Purchase lending, and surplus funds—one hundred thousand strings in each of the five major circuits, fifty thousand in the rest.

sentences.zh: 至是，復有是詔。

translations.literal: Reaching this time, again had this edict.
translations.idiomatic: The present edict reaffirmed that policy.

sentences.zh: 若無抵當而物貨宜易者，亦聽變鬻。

translations.literal: If no pawn yet goods suitable for trade, also permitted to change-sell.
translations.idiomatic: Goods suitable for resale but without collateral might still be sold off.

sentences.zh: 八年，罷諸鎮砦市易抵當。

translations.literal: Year 8, abolished all fortress-town Market Purchase pawn.
translations.idiomatic: In 1085, Market Purchase pawn offices in garrison towns were abolished.

sentences.zh: 八月，詔諸郡抵當，有取息薄、可濟民乏者存之，其餘抵當并州縣市易並罷。

translations.literal: Eighth month, an edict: various commandery pawn, those with thin interest able to help people's want—keep; rest of pawn and prefecture/county Market Purchase all abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, an edict preserved pawn offices in counties where low interest genuinely relieved the poor; all other pawn offices and county-level Market Purchase bureaus were shut down.

sentences.zh: 元祐元年，內外監督市易及坊場淨利錢，許以所入息並罰錢比計，若及官本者，並釋之。

translations.literal: Yuanyou year 1, inner and outer supervisors of Market Purchase and workshop net profit money, permitted to compare interest and penalty money received, if reaching official principal all released.
translations.idiomatic: In 1086, supervisors of Market Purchase and workshop franchises inside and outside the capital were allowed to offset interest and penalty payments against principal; debts satisfied to the official capital were forgiven.

sentences.zh: 紹聖四年，三省言熙寧興置市易，元祐一切罷去，不原立法之意。

translations.literal: Shaosheng year 4, Three Departments said Xining established Market Purchase, Yuanyou all abolished, did not return to original legislative intent.
translations.idiomatic: In 1097, the Three Departments observed that Market Purchase, created under Xining, had been entirely dismantled under Yuanyou in a way that betrayed the law's original purpose.

sentences.zh: 詔戶部、太府寺詳度，復置市易務，惟以錢交市，收息毋過二分，勿令貸請。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Finance Ministry, Palace Storehouse to examine, restore Market Purchase bureau, only with money exchange markets, interest not exceed two fen, do not permit lending requests.
translations.idiomatic: The Finance Ministry and Palace Storehouse were ordered to study restoration: Market Purchase offices would trade only in cash at no more than twenty per thousand interest, with lending prohibited.

sentences.zh: 元符三年，改市易務為平準務，戶部、太府寺市易案改為平準案。

translations.literal: Yuanfu year 3, changed Market Purchase bureau to Equilibrium bureau, Finance Market Purchase section changed to Equilibrium section.
translations.idiomatic: In 1100, Market Purchase bureaus became Equilibrium bureaus, and the related sections in the Finance Ministry and Palace Storehouse were renamed accordingly.

sentences.zh: 尚書省言：「平準務官吏等給費多，並遣官市物，搔動於外，近官鬻石炭，市直遽增，皆不便民。」

translations.literal: Ministry of Revenue said: "Equilibrium bureau officials' allowances many, also dispatching officials to market goods, disturbing outside, recently officials selling coal, market price suddenly rose, all inconvenient for people."
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Revenue reported that Equilibrium staff consumed too much in salaries, that dispatched buyers disrupted markets abroad, and that recent official coal sales had driven prices sharply up—all to the public's detriment.

sentences.zh: 詔罷平準務及官鬻石炭，其在官物貨，令有司轉易錢鈔，償元給之所。

translations.literal: An edict abolished Equilibrium bureau and official coal selling; its goods in government hands, ordered relevant offices to exchange into money notes, repay original disbursing places.
translations.idiomatic: The edict abolished the Equilibrium bureaus and official coal sales; remaining stock was to be liquidated for paper money and returned to the treasuries that had supplied the funds.

sentences.zh: 崇寧元年，戶部奏：平準務錢物毋得他司移用。

translations.literal: Chongning year 1, Finance Ministry memorialized: Equilibrium bureau money goods must not other bureaus transfer-use.
translations.idiomatic: In 1102, the Finance Ministry ruled that Equilibrium funds and goods could not be reallocated to other agencies.

sentences.zh: 二年，以平準為南北兩務，如舊分置官吏。

translations.literal: Year 2, made Equilibrium into north-south two bureaus, as before separately set officials.
translations.idiomatic: In 1103, the Equilibrium service was split into northern and southern bureaus with officials assigned as before.

sentences.zh: 歲終考察能否，行勸沮法。

translations.literal: Year end examined capability, implemented encourage-restrain law.
translations.idiomatic: Year-end reviews governed rewards and penalties under the encouragement-and-restraint rules.

sentences.zh: 五年，郡縣應置市易者，凡歲收息，官吏用度之餘，及千緡以上置官監，五百緡以上令場務兼領，餘並罷。

translations.literal: Year 5, commanderies and counties that should establish Market Purchase—annual interest after officials' expenses—1,000+ strings set official supervisor, 500+ strings ordered depot officials to concurrently lead, rest all abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In 1106, counties that still ran Market Purchase were tiered by annual profit after expenses: a thousand strings or more warranted a dedicated supervisor; five hundred or more, a depot officer's concurrent duty; below that, closure.

sentences.zh: 先是，嘗詔府界萬戶縣及路在衝要，市易抵當已設官置局；

translations.literal: Earlier, had issued an edict: capital district ten-thousand-household counties and routes at critical points, Market Purchase pawn already set officials and bureaus;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier edicts had required full Market Purchase and pawn offices in capital counties of ten thousand households or more and at strategic posts on the routes.

sentences.zh: 其不及萬戶、非衝要，並諸鎮有官監而商販所會，並如元豐令監當官兼領。

translations.literal: Those not reaching ten thousand households, not critical, also all towns with official supervision where merchants gathered—as Yuanfeng ordered, supervisor officials concurrently led.
translations.idiomatic: Smaller counties, non-critical stations, and market towns with existing garrison officers were to combine the duties under one Yuanyou-era supervisor as Jia Qing had arranged.

sentences.zh: 至是，戶部復詳度以聞，遂行其議。

translations.literal: Reaching this time, Finance Ministry again examined and reported, thereupon implemented the proposal.
translations.idiomatic: The Finance Ministry now reviewed and memorialized again, and the plan was carried out.

sentences.zh: 建炎二年，言者以為得不償費，遂罷之，而以其錢輸左藏庫，惟抵當庫仍舊。

translations.literal: Jianyan year 2, memorialists thought gains not repay costs, thereupon abolished, yet its money paid into Left Storehouse, only pawn treasury remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: In 1128, critics said the offices cost more than they earned; they were abolished and their funds sent to the Left Treasury, while pawn offices alone were kept.

sentences.zh: 紹興元年，罷諸州軍免行錢及行戶供應，見任官買賣並依時直，違者以盜論。

translations.literal: Shaoxing year 1, abolished all prefecture/army Exemption fees and Exemption household supply; incumbent officials buying-selling all per timely price, violators treated as theft.
translations.idiomatic: In 1131, Exemption fees and designated-supplier obligations were ended statewide; serving officials had to buy at market rates, with violations punished as theft.

sentences.zh: 四年，兩浙轉運司檄婺州市禦爐炭，須胡桃紋、鵓鳩色，守臣王居正以為言。

translations.literal: Year 4, Liangzhe transport commission ordered Wuzhou imperial furnace coal, requiring walnut grain, hawk-dove color, defender Wang Juzheng memorialized on it.
translations.idiomatic: In 1134, the Liangzhe transport commission demanded for Wuzhou imperial furnaces coal with walnut grain pattern and hawk-dove coloration; prefect Wang Juzheng objected.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「隆冬附火，取溫暖而已，豈問炭之紋色乎？」

translations.literal: Emperor said: "Deep winter seeking fire, taking warmth only—why ask coal's grain color?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "In midwinter one lights a brazier for warmth—who cares about the pattern on the coal?

sentences.zh: 命罷之，諸類此者並禁止焉。

translations.literal: Ordered abolish it, all such types also prohibited.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the requirement canceled and forbade similar demands henceforth.

sentences.zh: 十三年，蠲雷、化、高、融、宜、廉、邕、欽、賀、貴免行錢。

translations.literal: Year 13, remitted Lei, Hua, Gao, Rong, Yi, Lian, Yong, Qin, He, Gui Exemption fees.
translations.idiomatic: In 1143, Exemption fees were remitted in Leizhou, Huazhou, Gaozhou, Rongzhou, Yizhou, Lianzhou, Yongzhou, Qinzhou, Hezhou, and Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 十四年，以開州兩縣在夔部尤為僻遠，減免行錢之半。

translations.literal: Year 14, because Kaizhou two counties in Kuai region especially remote, reduced Exemption fee by half.
translations.idiomatic: In 1144, the two counties of Kaizhou in the Kuai region, being exceptionally remote, had their Exemption fees cut by half.

sentences.zh: 十五年，以知漢陽軍韓昕言，諸路收免行錢，定數外多取一文以上，以擅增稅賦法罪之。

translations.literal: Year 15, following Han Xin military prefect of Hanyang's statement, various circuits collecting Exemption fees—outside fixed amount taking one cash more—punished by unauthorized tax increase law.
translations.idiomatic: In 1145, after Han Xin, prefect of Hanyang, warned that any circuit collecting more than one cash above the fixed Exemption fee would be charged under the law against unauthorized levies.

sentences.zh: 十七年，蠲百姓見輸免行錢三分之一。

translations.literal: Year 17, remitted common people's current Exemption fee payment one-third.
translations.idiomatic: In 1147, one-third of current Exemption fees owed by the people was remitted.

sentences.zh: 十九年，南郊赦，盡蠲百姓免行錢欠。

translations.literal: Year 19, southern suburb amnesty, fully remitted people's Exemption fee arrears.
translations.idiomatic: The 1149 southern suburban amnesty canceled all outstanding Exemption fees.

sentences.zh: 是後凡赦皆然。

translations.literal: Thereafter every amnesty was likewise.
translations.idiomatic: Every subsequent amnesty did the same.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，罷見輸免行錢，禁下行買物，以害及小商、敷於鄉村故也。

translations.literal: Year 25, abolished current Exemption fee payment, banned going down to buy goods, because harm reached small merchants, imposed on villages.
translations.idiomatic: In 1155, current Exemption fees were abolished and lower officials were forbidden to requisition goods locally, because the practice had hurt peddlers and burdened the countryside.

sentences.zh: 淳熙元年，罷市令司。

translations.literal: Chunxi year 1, abolished Market Magistrate bureau.
translations.idiomatic: In 1174, the Market Magistrate bureau was abolished.

sentences.zh: 詔臨安府及屬縣交易儈保錢減十之五。

translations.literal: An edict: Lin'an prefecture and subordinate counties' trade broker-guarantee money reduced five of ten.
translations.idiomatic: Broker-guarantee fees in Lin'an and its counties were cut by half.

sentences.zh: 七年，諸路州縣交易儈保錢，亦以十分為率，與減五分。

translations.literal: Year 7, all circuits' prefecture/county trade broker-guarantee money, also using ten parts as rate, likewise reduced five parts.
translations.idiomatic: In 1180, circuit broker-guarantee fees were likewise cut by fifty percent.

sentences.zh: 嘉定二年，以臣僚言，輦轂之下，買物於鋪戶，無從得錢。

translations.literal: Jiading year 2, following civil officials' words, under the carriage-and-hub, buying goods from shops, no way to get money.
translations.idiomatic: In 1209, officials reported that in the capital, shops supplying government purchases could not obtain payment.

sentences.zh: 凡臨安府未支物價，令即日盡數給還，是後買物須給見錢，違許陳訴於台。

translations.literal: All Lin'an prefecture unpaid goods prices, ordered same day full amount repaid; thereafter buying goods must give ready money, violators permitted to appeal at the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: All unpaid Lin'an purchase debts were to be settled at once; thereafter cash on delivery was mandatory, with appeals to the Censorate for violations.

sentences.zh: 嘉熙三年，臣僚言：「今官司以官價買物，行鋪以時直計之，什不得二三。

translations.literal: Jiaxi year 3, officials said: "Now government offices with official price buy goods, shops with timely price calculate—ten parts not reaching two-three.
translations.idiomatic: In 1239, officials reported: "Agencies now pay official schedule prices, while shops reckon at market rates—so merchants receive barely twenty or thirty percent of fair value.

sentences.zh: 重以遷延歲月而不償，胥卒並緣之無藝，積日既久，類成白著，至有遷居以避其擾、改業以逃其害者。

translations.literal: Added to delaying months and years without repayment, clerks and soldiers together exploited without limit, days piled long, type becoming white-bestowal, even some relocating to avoid harassment, changing trade to escape harm.
translations.idiomatic: Payment is delayed for months or years while clerks and runners extort without limit; debts become outright confiscation. Some merchants move away or change trades to escape.

sentences.zh: 甚而蔬菜魚肉，日用所需瑣瑣之物，販夫販婦所資錐刀以營斗升者，亦皆以官價強取之。

translations.literal: Even vegetables fish meat, daily needed trifling things, peddler men and women relying on knife's edge to earn dou and sheng, also all with official price forcibly taken.
translations.idiomatic: Even vegetables, fish, and meat—the petty goods of hawkers who live on pennies a day—are seized at official prices.

sentences.zh: 終日營營，而錢本俱成乾沒。

translations.literal: All day toiling, yet capital and principal all become dry embezzlement.
translations.idiomatic: They toil all day yet never recover principal or profit.

sentences.zh: 商旅不行，衣食路絕。

translations.literal: Traveling merchants do not travel, food and clothing roads cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Traveling merchants stop coming; livelihoods are cut off.

sentences.zh: 望特降睿旨，凡諸路州縣官司買物，並以時直；

translations.literal: Hope specially descend sagely order, all circuits' prefecture/county government offices buying goods, all at timely price;
translations.idiomatic: We beg a special edict that every prefecture and county purchase at market price;

sentences.zh: 不許輒用官價，違者以贓定罪。」

translations.literal: not permit rashly using official price, violators by embezzlement fix crime."
translations.idiomatic: and that use of official schedule prices be forbidden, violations punished as graft."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: Followed.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 均輸之法，所以通天下之貨，制為輕重斂散之術，使輸者既便，而有無得以懋遷焉。

translations.literal: Balanced Transport law—that by which circulates under-heaven's goods, fashioned as light-heavy gather-disperse technique, making submitters already convenient, and having-not having obtain flourishing exchange.
translations.idiomatic: Balanced Transport was meant to move goods throughout the empire, regulating abundance and scarcity so that suppliers were unburdened and surplus and shortage could be actively redressed.

sentences.zh: 熙寧二年，製置三司條例司言：「天下財用無餘，典領之官拘於弊法，內外不相知，盈虛不相補。

translations.literal: Xining year 2, Fiscal Reform Commission said: "Under-heaven finances without surplus, overseeing officials constrained by corrupt methods, inner and outer do not know each other, surplus and deficit do not supplement.
translations.idiomatic: In 1069, the Fiscal Reform Commission reported: "National revenue is exhausted. Controllers are trapped in obsolete rules; capital and provinces do not coordinate, and surplus and deficit are never balanced.

sentences.zh: 諸路上供，歲有常數。

translations.literal: Various circuits' upward tribute, yearly have fixed numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Each circuit's annual tribute quota is fixed.

sentences.zh: 豐年便道，可以多致而不能贏；

translations.literal: Abundant years convenient routes, can deliver more yet cannot win surplus;
translations.idiomatic: In good years convenient routes could yield more than the quota, but the surplus could not be retained;

sentences.zh: 年儉物貴，難於供億而不敢不足。

translations.literal: Lean years goods dear, hard to supply in full yet dare not be insufficient.
translations.idiomatic: in lean years when goods were dear, delivery was hard yet shortfall was not permitted.

sentences.zh: 遠方有倍蓰之輸，中都有半價之鬻，徒使富商大賈乘公私之急，以擅輕重斂散之權。

translations.literal: Far regions have doubled-tripled tribute, capital has half-price selling, vainly letting great wealthy merchants ride public-private urgency, to monopolize light-heavy gather-disperse power.
translations.idiomatic: Remote regions pay multiples while the capital sells at half price, leaving great merchants alone to profit from public and private distress and monopolize the power to manipulate prices.

sentences.zh: 今發運使實總六路賦入，其職以製置茶、鹽、礬、酒稅為事，軍儲國用，多所仰給。

translations.literal: Now Dispatch Commissioner in fact oversees six circuits' tax intake, his duty to arrange tea, salt, alum, wine taxes; military stores national use, much relies on his supply.
translations.idiomatic: The Dispatch Commissioner already oversees tax intake from the six circuits and manages tea, salt, alum, and wine levies on which military stores and the civil budget largely depend.

sentences.zh: 宜假以錢貨，資其用度，周知六路財賦之有無而移用之。

translations.literal: Should lend him money goods, fund his expenditures, comprehensively know six circuits' wealth's having-not and transfer-use it.
translations.idiomatic: He should be given capital, informed of every circuit's resources, and empowered to shift funds where needed.

sentences.zh: 凡糴買稅斂上供之物，皆得徙貴就賤，用近易遠。

translations.literal: All grain-buying tax-collecting upward tribute goods, all may move from dear to cheap, use near replace far.
translations.idiomatic: All tribute goods—whether purchased or levied—might be procured where cheap rather than dear and nearby rather than distant.

sentences.zh: 令預知中都帑藏年支見在之定數，所當供辦者，得以從便變易蓄買，以待上令。

translations.literal: Order him beforehand to know capital treasury yearly disbursement on-hand fixed numbers, what ought to be supplied—obtain from-convenience change-store buy, to await superior orders.
translations.idiomatic: Foreknowing the capital treasury's annual outlays and reserves, he could stockpile and trade flexibly until orders came from above.

sentences.zh: 稍收輕重斂散之權歸之公上，而制其有無，以便轉輸，省勞費，去重斂，寬農民。

translations.literal: Slightly recover light-heavy gather-disperse power return to public above, and control its having-not, to facilitate transport, save labor costs, remove heavy levies, widen farmers.
translations.idiomatic: The state would gradually reclaim control over supply and demand, ease transport, cut costs, lift excessive levies, and relieve farmers.

sentences.zh: 庶幾國用可足，民財不匱。」

translations.literal: Perhaps national use can suffice, people's wealth not exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the treasury might be filled without exhausting the people.

sentences.zh: 詔本司具條例以聞，而以發運使薛向領均輸平準事，賜內藏錢五百萬緡、上供米三百萬石。

translations.literal: An edict ordered this bureau to prepare regulations and report; and made Dispatch Commissioner Xue Xiang lead Balanced Transport Equilibrium affairs, bestowed inner treasury money 5 million strings, tribute rice 3 million shi.
translations.idiomatic: The commission was ordered to draft regulations. Xue Xiang, the Dispatch Commissioner, was placed in charge of Balanced Transport and price stabilization, with five million strings from the inner treasury and three million shi of tribute grain.

sentences.zh: 時議慮其為擾，多以為非。

translations.literal: Contemporary discussion feared it would be disturbance, many thought it wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Critics feared disruption, and opposition was widespread.

sentences.zh: 向既董其事，乃請設置官屬，神宗使自擇之。

translations.literal: Xiang having supervised the affair, then requested setting up staff; Shenzong let him self-select.
translations.idiomatic: Once in charge, Xue requested staff; Shenzong let him choose his own aides.

sentences.zh: 向於是辟劉忱、衛琪、孫珪、張穆之、陳倩為屬，又請有司具六路歲當上供數、中都歲用及見儲度可支歲月，凡當計置歲何，皆預降有司。

translations.literal: Xiang thereupon recruited Liu Chen, Wei Qi, Sun Gui, Zhang Muzhi, Chen Qian as staff; also requested relevant offices prepare six circuits' yearly due tribute, capital yearly use and on-hand storage degree of months supportable, all matters for planning which year—all beforehand deliver to relevant offices.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Liu Chen, Wei Qi, Sun Gui, Zhang Muzhi, and Chen Qian as deputies and required agencies to submit the six circuits' annual tribute quotas, capital expenditures, and reserves—every figure needed for yearly planning.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: Followed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 八月，侍御史劉琦、侍御史裏行錢顗等言：「向小人，假以貨泉，任其變易，縱有所入，不免奪商賈之利。」

translations.literal: Eighth month, Attending Censor Liu Qi, Attending Censor trainee Qian Yi etc. said: "Xiang is petty man, lent money strings, let him change-trade, even if some intake, cannot avoid seizing merchants' profit.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, Attending Censor Liu Qi and trainee Attending Censor Qian Yi memorialized: "Xue Xiang is unworthy. Lending him state funds to trade at will may bring revenue but will only strip merchants of their profits."

sentences.zh: 琦、顗皆坐貶。

translations.literal: Qi and Yi both sat demoted.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qi and Qian Yi were both demoted for their remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 條例司檢詳文字蘇轍言：「昔漢武外事四夷，內興宮室，財用匱竭，力不能支，用賈人桑弘羊之說，買賤賣貴，謂之均輸。

translations.literal: Commission text reviewer Su Zhe said: "Formerly Han Wu foreign affairs four barbarians, inner raised palaces, finances exhausted, strength could not support, used merchant Sang Hongyang's plan, buy cheap sell dear, called Balanced Transport.
translations.idiomatic: Su Zhe of the commission staff wrote: "Under Emperor Wu, wars abroad and palaces at home exhausted the treasury. He adopted the merchant Sang Hongyang's scheme—buy cheap, sell dear—called Balanced Transport.

sentences.zh: 雖曰民不加賦而國用饒足，然法術不正，吏緣為奸，掊克日深，民受其病。

translations.literal: Although said people not add levies yet national use rich full, yet methods not correct, clerks exploited as treachery, extortion daily deeper, people received its harm.
translations.idiomatic: Though marketed as adding no levies while filling the state, the method was unsound. Officials preyed on it; extortion deepened daily and the people bore the wound.

sentences.zh: 孝昭既立，學者爭排其說，霍光順民所欲，從而予之，天下歸心，遂以無事。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhao having risen, scholars contended to reject his doctrine, Huo Guang followed people's desire, from this granted it, under-heaven returned hearts, thereupon without incident.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Zhao's accession, scholars denounced the policy; Huo Guang followed the people's wish and abolished it; the realm's hearts returned and peace followed.

sentences.zh: 今此論復興，眾口紛然，皆謂其患必甚於漢。

translations.literal: Now this doctrine again rises, many mouths clamorous, all say its harm necessarily exceeds Han.
translations.idiomatic: Now the policy revives amid widespread outcry that its harms will surely exceed those of Han times.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: How so?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 方今聚斂之臣，材智方略，未見有桑弘羊比；

translations.literal: Now among revenue-gathering ministers, in talent, wit, and stratagem, none is seen to match Sang Hongyang;
translations.idiomatic: Among today's revenue-minded officials, none approaches Sang Hongyang in ability or design;

sentences.zh: 而朝廷破壞規矩，解縱繩墨，使得馳騁自由，唯利是嗜，其害必有不可勝言者矣。」

translations.literal: yet the court destroys rules, loosens measuring cords, lets them gallop freely, craving profit alone—the harm surely has what cannot be told in full."
translations.idiomatic: yet the court has torn down the guardrails and turned them loose to chase profit alone, and the damage will surely prove beyond reckoning."

sentences.zh: 轍亦坐去官。

translations.literal: Su Zhe also by association was removed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Su Zhe too was dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 於是知諫院範純仁言：「向憸巧刻薄，不可為發運使。

translations.literal: Thereupon Remonstrance Bureau director Fan Chunren said: " Xiang is crafty and mean, unfit to be transport commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Then Fan Chunren, head of the Remonstrance Bureau, said, "Xue Xiang is sly and harsh—he must not serve as transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 人主當務農桑、節用，不當言利。」

translations.literal: The ruler ought to devote himself to farming and sericulture, economize expenditure, and ought not speak of profit."
translations.idiomatic: A sovereign should promote agriculture and thrift, not profit."

sentences.zh: 自後，罷純仁諫職，而諫官李常復論均輸不便，權開封府推官蘇軾亦言：「均輸徙貴就賤，用近易遠。

translations.literal: After this Fan Chunren's remonstrance post was ended; remonstrance officer Li Chang again argued Balanced Transport's inconvenience; acting Kaifeng prefectural investigator Su Shi also said: " Balanced Transport moves dear toward cheap, uses the near to ease the far.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Chunren was removed from the remonstrance post. Li Chang again attacked Balanced Transport as unworkable. Su Shi, acting Kaifeng investigator, said, "Balanced Transport shifts goods from dear to cheap markets and favors the near over the far—

sentences.zh: 然廣置官屬，多出緡錢，豪商大賈皆疑而不敢動，以為雖不明言販賣，既已許之變易，變易既行，而不與商賈爭利，未之聞也。

translations.literal: yet offices are broadly staffed and much string-cash spent; great merchants all hesitate and dare not act, thinking that though trade is not openly named, exchange is already permitted—once exchange proceeds, not competing with merchants for profit is something never heard of.
translations.idiomatic: yet it staffs a vast bureaucracy and spends heavily in cash, so great merchants hang back in suspicion: though buying and selling are not named outright, exchange is authorized—and once the state trades, who has ever heard of it not competing with merchants for profit?

sentences.zh: 夫商賈之事，曲折難行，其買也先期而予錢，其賣也後期而取直，多方相濟，委曲相通，倍稱之息，由此而得。

translations.literal: As for merchants' affairs, they twist and are hard to execute: in buying they advance payment beforehand; in selling they take price afterward; many parties assist one another, winding paths connect, doubled interest is thereby obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Commerce runs on tangled, delicate practice: buyers pay in advance, sellers collect later, parties help one another through twists of credit—and doubled returns come from that art.

sentences.zh: 今先設官置吏，簿書廩祿，為費已厚，非良不售，非賄不行。

translations.literal: Now officials and clerks are set up first; ledgers and salaries make costs already heavy—without quality nothing sells, without bribes nothing moves.
translations.idiomatic: Now the state erects offices and clerks first; ledgers and salaries already swell the cost—goods won't move without quality, deals won't close without bribes.

sentences.zh: 是官買之價比民必貴，及其賣也，弊復如前，商賈之利，何緣而得？

translations.literal: Thus government purchase prices compared with the people's must be dear; when it comes to selling, abuses return as before—by what path can merchants' profit be obtained?
translations.idiomatic: Official purchase prices must exceed private ones; when the state sells, the old abuses return—how can merchants still earn?

sentences.zh: 朝廷不知慮此，乃捐五百萬緡以予之。

translations.literal: The court did not consider this, yet donated five million strings of cash to grant them.
translations.idiomatic: The court ignored these concerns and handed over five million strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 此錢一出，恐不可復。

translations.literal: Once this money goes out, I fear it cannot return.
translations.idiomatic: Once that money is spent, it may never come back.

sentences.zh: 縱使其間薄有所獲，而征商之額所損必多矣。」

translations.literal: Even if in the interval they gain a little, the amount lost from merchant levies must be great."
translations.idiomatic: Even if the scheme yields a little, the loss in commercial tax revenue will surely be far greater."

sentences.zh: 帝方惑於安石之說，言皆不行。

translations.literal: The emperor was then bewildered by Wang Anshi's doctrine; all such words went unheeded.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was still swayed by Wang Anshi's views, and none of these remonstrances took effect.

sentences.zh: 乃以向為天章閣待制，遣太常少卿羅拯為使，手詔賜向曰：「政事之先，理財為急。

translations.literal: Thereupon Xiang was made Hanlin associate academician of the Tianzhang Pavilion; Vice Minister of Rites Luo Zheng was sent as envoy; an autograph edict granted to Xiang said: " In government affairs, first comes finance—managing wealth is urgent.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Xiang was made a Tianzhang Pavilion academician; Vice Minister of Rites Luo Zheng was dispatched with a personal edict: "In governance, finance comes first—managing revenue is urgent.

sentences.zh: 朕托卿以東南賦入，皆得消息盈虛、翕張斂散之。

translations.literal: We entrust you with the southeast's tax intake, that you may grasp fullness and emptiness, expansion and contraction, gathering and dispersal.
translations.idiomatic: We entrust you with the southeast's revenue so you may master its ebb and flow—when to gather and when to release.

sentences.zh: 而卿忠誠內固，能倡舉職業，導揚朕意，底於成績，朕甚嘉之。

translations.literal: You, loyal and firm within, can initiate and raise your duties, guide and spread Our intent, reach achievement—We greatly commend this.
translations.idiomatic: Your loyalty runs deep; you have led the work forward and carried out Our intent to real results—We commend you warmly.

sentences.zh: 覽奏慮流言致惑，朕心匪石，豈易轉也？

translations.literal: Reading your memorial, you worry slander may cause confusion—Our heart is not stone; how could it easily turn?
translations.idiomatic: In your memorial you fear rumor may sow doubt—Our resolve is not stone, easily shifted.

sentences.zh: 卿其濟之以強，終之以不倦，以稱朕意。」

translations.literal: You should aid it with strength, finish it without weariness, to match Our intent."
translations.idiomatic: Press on with force, finish without fatigue, and fulfill Our intent."

sentences.zh: 然均輸後迄不能成。

translations.literal: Yet Balanced Transport afterward to the end could not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Balanced Transport never came to fruition.

sentences.zh: 互市舶法自漢初與南越通關市，而互市之制行焉。

translations.literal: Mutual-border markets and seaborne-trade law: from early Han, when border markets were opened with Nanyue, the mutual-market system was put in practice.
translations.idiomatic: Mutual border markets and maritime trade regulations began in early Han, when frontier trade with Nanyue opened and the mutual-market system took shape.

sentences.zh: 後漢通交易於烏桓、北單于、鮮卑，北魏立互市於南陲，隋、唐通貿易於西北。

translations.literal: Later Han opened exchange with Wuhuan, the Northern Chanyu, and Xianbei; Northern Wei established mutual markets on the southern marches; Sui and Tang opened trade on the northwest.
translations.idiomatic: Later Han traded with the Wuhuan, Northern Chanyu, and Xianbei; Northern Wei set mutual markets on the southern frontier; Sui and Tang extended trade into the northwest.

sentences.zh: 開元定令，載其條目，後唐亦然。

translations.literal: The Kaiyuan statutes fixed the rules and recorded their articles; Later Tang did likewise.
translations.idiomatic: The Kaiyuan code codified the articles; Later Tang followed the same pattern.

sentences.zh: 而高麗、回鶻、黑水諸國，又各以風土所產與中國交易。

translations.literal: Koryŏ, Uyghur, Heishui, and other states each also traded with China in what their lands produced.
translations.idiomatic: Koryŏ, the Uyghurs, Heishui Mohe, and others likewise traded native products with China.

sentences.zh: 宋初，循周制，與江南通市。

translations.literal: At the Song's beginning, following Zhou practice, markets were opened with Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Song, following Zhou precedent, trade continued with Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 乾德二年，禁商旅毋得渡江，於建安、漢陽、蘄口置三榷署，通其交易；

translations.literal: Qiande year 2, merchants were forbidden to cross the river; at Jian'an, Hanyang, and Qikou three monopoly offices were set up to channel their trade;
translations.idiomatic: In 964 merchants were barred from crossing the Yangzi freely; three monopoly bureaus at Jian'an, Hanyang, and Qikou regulated exchange;

sentences.zh: 內外群臣輒遣人往江、浙販易者，沒入其貨。

translations.literal: court and local officials who rashly sent people to Jiang and Zhe to trade had their goods confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: officials who sent agents to trade in Jiangsu and Zhejiang had their goods seized.

sentences.zh: 緣江百姓及煎鹽亭戶，恣其樵漁，所造屨席之類，榷署給券，聽渡江販易。

translations.literal: River-bank commoners and salt-boiling households were free to gather fuel and fish; sandals, mats, and the like they made—the monopoly office issued passes, allowing them to cross and trade.
translations.idiomatic: River folk and salt-furnace households could gather wood and fish; for sandals, mats, and similar goods the monopoly office issued permits to cross and sell.

sentences.zh: 開寶三年，徙建安榷署於揚州。

translations.literal: Kaibao year 3, the Jian'an monopoly office was moved to Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In 970 the Jian'an monopoly office was relocated to Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 江南平，榷署雖存，止掌茶貨。

translations.literal: When Jiangnan was pacified, though the monopoly offices remained, they handled only tea goods.
translations.idiomatic: After Jiangnan fell, the bureaus remained but managed only tea.

sentences.zh: 四年，置市舶司於廣州，後又於杭、明州置司。

translations.literal: Year 4, the Maritime Trade Office was established at Guangzhou; later offices were also set at Hang and Ming prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In 971 Guangzhou gained a Maritime Trade Office; Hangzhou and Mingzhou followed.

sentences.zh: 凡大食、古邏、闍婆、占城、勃泥、麻逸、三佛齋諸蕃並通貨易，以金銀、緡錢、鉛錫、雜色帛、瓷器，市香藥、犀象、珊瑚、琥珀、珠琲、镔鐵、鼊皮、玳瑁、瑪瑙、車渠、水精、蕃布、烏樠、蘇木等物。

translations.literal: All the fan of Dashi, Gulu, Zabag, Champa, Brunei, Mayi, Sanfoqi, and the like traded goods, offering gold and silver, string-cash, lead and tin, assorted silks, and porcelain to buy aromatics, rhinoceros and ivory, coral, amber, pearls, wootz iron, ray hides, tortoiseshell, agate, giant-clam shell, crystal, foreign cloth, eaglewood, sappanwood, and such articles.
translations.idiomatic: Peoples from Dashi, Gulu, Java, Champa, Brunei, the Philippines, Srivijaya, and beyond traded with China, paying in gold, silver, cash, lead, tin, colored silks, and porcelain for aromatics, ivory, coral, amber, pearls, steel, ray skin, tortoiseshell, agate, giant-clam shell, crystal, foreign cloth, eaglewood, sappanwood, and the like.

sentences.zh: 太宗時，置榷署於京師，詔諸蕃香藥寶貨至廣州、交阯、兩浙、泉州，非出官庫者，無得私相貿易。

translations.literal: Under Taizong, a monopoly office was set in the capital; an edict said aromatics and treasure goods of the fan arriving at Guangzhou, Jiaozhi, the two Zhe circuits, and Quanzhou might not be privately traded except through the state storehouses.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong placed a monopoly office in the capital and decreed that foreign aromatics and treasure reaching Guangzhou, Jiaozhi, the two Zhe circuits, and Quanzhou could not be traded privately outside the official warehouses.

sentences.zh: 其後乃詔：「自今惟珠貝、玳瑁、犀象、镔鐵、鼊皮、珊瑚、瑪瑙、乳香禁榷外，他藥官市之餘，聽市於民。」

translations.literal: Afterward an edict said: " From now only pearls and shells, tortoiseshell, rhinoceros and ivory, wootz iron, ray hide, coral, agate, and frankincense are forbidden monopoly; other drugs, after the state's purchase, may be sold to the people."
translations.idiomatic: Later an edict ruled: "Henceforth only pearls, tortoiseshell, ivory, wootz steel, ray skin, coral, agate, and frankincense remain state monopolies; other aromatics, after official purchase, may be sold to private buyers."

sentences.zh: 雍熙中，遣內侍八人齎敕書金帛，分四路招致海南諸蕃。

translations.literal: In the Yongxi era, eight inner attendants were sent bearing imperial letters, gold, and silks, divided into four routes to summon the southern-sea fan.
translations.idiomatic: During Yongxi (984–987), eight palace eunuchs carried imperial letters, gold, and silks along four routes to invite southern maritime traders.

sentences.zh: 商人出海外蕃國販易者，令並詣兩浙司市舶司請給官券，違者沒入其寶貨。

translations.literal: Merchants going abroad to fan states to trade were ordered all to go to the two-Zhe Maritime Trade Office to request official passes; violators had their treasure goods confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: Merchants sailing overseas had to obtain official permits from the Zhe maritime office; violators forfeited their cargo.

sentences.zh: 淳熙二年，詔廣州市舶，除榷貨外，他貨之良者止市其半。

translations.literal: Chunxi year 2, an edict on Guangzhou maritime trade: aside from monopoly goods, of other goods only half the fine grade was to be purchased by the state.
translations.idiomatic: In 1175 Guangzhou was ordered: beyond monopoly items, the state would buy only half of the best grade of other goods.

sentences.zh: 大抵海船至，十先征其一，價直酌蕃貨輕重而差給之，歲約獲五十餘萬斤、條、株、顆。

translations.literal: Generally when seagoing ships arrived, one in ten was levied first; price and value were adjusted to the fan goods' weight and lightness and differentially paid—yearly intake was about five hundred thousand-plus jin, strips, stalks, and pieces.
translations.idiomatic: As a rule, one-tenth of incoming cargo was levied first; payment varied with the weight and value of foreign goods, yielding yearly some five hundred thousand units by weight, strip, stalk, or piece.

sentences.zh: 太平興國初，私與蕃國人貿易者，計直滿百錢以上論罪，十五貫以上黥麵流海島，過此送闕下。

translations.literal: Early Taiping Xingguo, those who privately traded with fan peoples: valued at one hundred cash or more were punished; at fifteen strings or more, face tattooed and exiled to sea islands; beyond that, sent to court.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taiping Xingguo (976–978), private trade with foreigners was criminal from one hundred cash upward; at fifteen strings, offenders were tattooed and exiled to island penal colonies; larger cases went to the capital.

sentences.zh: 淳化五年申其禁，至四貫以上徒一年，稍加至二十貫以上，黥麵配本州為役兵。

translations.literal: Chunhua year 5 tightened the ban: at four strings or more, penal servitude one year; gradually increased to twenty strings or more—face tattooed and assigned within the prefecture as corvée soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: In 994 the ban was tightened: four strings brought one year's penal servitude, rising to tattooing and assignment as corvée troops in the home prefecture at twenty strings.

sentences.zh: 天聖以來，象犀、珠玉、香藥、寶貨充刃府庫，嘗斥其餘以易金帛、芻粟，縣官用度實有助焉。

translations.literal: From Tiansheng onward, ivory, rhinoceros horn, pearls, jade, aromatics, and treasure filled the government stores; surplus was sometimes sold off for gold, silks, and fodder-grain—the state's expenditures were truly aided.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Tiansheng era (1023–1031), ivory, rhino horn, pearls, jade, aromatics, and treasure packed the treasuries; surpluses were traded for gold, silk, and grain, materially easing state spending.

sentences.zh: 而官市貨數，視淳化則微有所損。

translations.literal: Yet the quantity of goods the state purchased was slightly less compared with Chunhua.
translations.idiomatic: Official purchase volumes, however, fell slightly below Chunhua levels.

sentences.zh: 皇祐中，總歲入象犀、珠玉、香藥之類，其數五十三萬有餘。

translations.literal: In Huangyou, total yearly intake of ivory, rhinoceros horn, pearls, jade, aromatics, and the like numbered five hundred thirty thousand-odd.
translations.idiomatic: Under Huangyou (1049–1053), annual intake of ivory, rhino horn, pearls, jade, and aromatics totaled over five hundred thirty thousand units.

sentences.zh: 至治平中，又增十萬。

translations.literal: By Zhiping it increased another one hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: By the Zhiping era (1064–1067) the figure rose another hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 熙寧五年，詔發運使薛向曰：「東南之利，舶商居其一。

translations.literal: Xining year 5, an edict to Transport Commissioner Xue Xiang said: " The southeast's profit—maritime merchants hold one share.
translations.idiomatic: In 1072 the throne told Transport Commissioner Xue Xiang, "Of the southeast's revenue, maritime trade is a major share—

sentences.zh: 比言者請置司泉州，其創法講求之。」

translations.literal: Recently remonstrators asked to establish an office at Quanzhou—study and pursue its founding methods."
translations.idiomatic: remonstrators have urged opening an office at Quanzhou; investigate and draft the regulations.

sentences.zh: 七年，令舶船遇風至諸州界，亟報所隸，送近地舶司榷賦分買；

translations.literal: Year 7, ordered that when merchant ships met wind and reached any prefectural border, they quickly report to their jurisdiction and be sent to the nearest maritime office for levy, apportionment, and divided purchase;
translations.idiomatic: In 1074 storm-driven ships reaching any prefecture had to report at once to local authorities and proceed to the nearest maritime office for levy and shared purchase;

sentences.zh: 泉、福瀕海舟船未經賦買者，仍赴司勘驗。

translations.literal: Quan and Fu coastal ships that had not yet undergone levy and purchase still had to go to the office for inspection.
translations.idiomatic: vessels from Quanzhou and Fuzhou that had not yet been levied still had to report to the office for inspection.

sentences.zh: 時廣州市舶虧歲課二十萬緡，或以為市易司擾之，故海商不至，令提舉司究詰以聞。

translations.literal: At the time Guangzhou maritime trade was short two hundred thousand strings in yearly revenue; some thought the Market Exchange Office disturbed it, so sea merchants did not come—the investigating commission was ordered to examine and report.
translations.idiomatic: Guangzhou's maritime revenue then fell short by two hundred thousand strings; some blamed harassment by the Market Exchange Office, which kept merchants away—the investigating commission was ordered to inquire and report.

sentences.zh: 既而市易務呂邈入舶司闌取蕃商物，詔提舉司劾之。

translations.literal: Soon after, Market Exchange clerk Lü Miao entered the maritime office and forcibly seized fan merchants' goods; the investigating commission was ordered to impeach him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Lü Miao of the Market Exchange Office entered the maritime bureau and seized foreign merchants' goods by force; the investigating commission was ordered to prosecute him.

sentences.zh: 九年，集賢殿修撰程師孟請罷杭、明州市舶，諸舶皆隸廣州一司。

translations.literal: Year 9, Hanlin compiler Cheng Shimeng requested abolishing Hang and Ming maritime offices—all shipping to be subordinate to Guangzhou alone.
translations.idiomatic: In 1076 Hanlin compiler Cheng Shimeng proposed closing the Hangzhou and Mingzhou maritime offices and placing all trade under Guangzhou alone.

sentences.zh: 令師孟與三司詳議之。

translations.literal: Cheng Shimeng and the Three Departments were ordered to deliberate in detail.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Shimeng and the fiscal Three Departments were told to study the plan.

sentences.zh: 是年，杭、明、廣三司市舶，收錢、糧、銀、香、藥等五十四萬一百七十三緡、匹、斤、兩、段、條、個、顆、臍、隻、粒，支二十三萬八千五十六緡、匹、斤、兩、段、條、個、顆、臍、隻、粒。

translations.literal: That year the Hang, Ming, and Guang maritime offices took in cash, grain, silver, aromatics, drugs, and the like totaling 541,073 strings, bolts, jin, taels, lengths, strips, pieces, kernels, navels, animals, and grains; they disbursed 238,056 in the same units.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Hangzhou, Mingzhou, and Guangzhou offices recorded receipts of 541,073 units (strings, bolts, pounds, taels, lengths, pieces, and the like) in cash, grain, silver, aromatics, and drugs, and expenditures of 238,056 units.

sentences.zh: 元豐二年，賈人入高麗，資及五千緡者，明州籍其名，歲責保給引發船，無引者如盜販法。

translations.literal: Yuankeng year 2, merchants going to Koryŏ with capital reaching five thousand strings—Mingzhou registered their names, yearly requiring guarantors to issue permits before sailing; without a permit, the law on illicit trade applied.
translations.idiomatic: In 1079 merchants sailing to Koryŏ with capital of five thousand strings or more were registered at Mingzhou; each year guarantors had to issue sailing permits—without one, smuggling penalties applied.

sentences.zh: 先是，禁人私販，然不能絕；

translations.literal: Earlier, private trade had been forbidden, yet it could not be ended;
translations.idiomatic: Private trade had long been banned, yet it could not be stamped out;

sentences.zh: 至是，復通中國，故明立是法。

translations.literal: now trade with China was restored, hence this law was clearly established.
translations.idiomatic: now that commerce with China had reopened, the rule was set forth in explicit form.

sentences.zh: 三年，中書言，廣州市舶已修定條約，宜選官推行。

translations.literal: Year 3, the Secretariat said Guangzhou maritime trade had revised and fixed its regulations—it was fitting to select officials to implement them.
translations.idiomatic: In 1080 the Secretariat reported that Guangzhou's maritime regulations had been revised and officials should be chosen to enforce them.

sentences.zh: 詔廣東以轉運使孫迥，廣西以陳倩，兩浙以副使周直孺，福建以判官王子京，罷廣東帥臣兼領。

translations.literal: An edict: Guangdong—Transport Commissioner Sun Jiong; Guangxi—Chen Qian; two Zhe—Vice Commissioner Zhou Zhiru; Fujian—Judge Wang Zijing; the Guangdong military commander's concurrent charge was ended.
translations.idiomatic: Guangdong was assigned to Transport Commissioner Sun Jiong, Guangxi to Chen Qian, the two Zhe circuits to Vice Commissioner Zhou Zhiru, Fujian to Judge Wang Zijing—and the Guangdong commander's concurrent oversight was abolished.

sentences.zh: 五年，廣西漕臣吳潛言：「雷、化州與瓊島對境，而發船請引於廣州舶司，約五千里。

translations.literal: Year 5, Guangxi transport official Wu Qian said: " Lei and Hua prefectures face Qiong Island across the sea, yet to sail they must request permits at Guangzhou's maritime office—about five thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: In 1082 Guangxi transport commissioner Wu Qian said, "Lei and Hua prefectures lie opposite Hainan, yet ships must travel some five thousand li to Guangzhou for sailing permits—

sentences.zh: 乞令廣西瀕海郡縣，土著商人載米穀、牛酒、黃魚及非舶司賦取之物，免至廣州請引。」

translations.literal: We beg that Guangxi's coastal commanderies and counties allow native merchants carrying grain, cattle, wine, yellow fish, and goods not subject to maritime-office levy to be exempt from going to Guangzhou for permits."
translations.idiomatic: allow Guangxi coastal counties to let local merchants carrying grain, cattle, wine, yellow croaker, and goods not subject to maritime levy sail without Guangzhou permits."

sentences.zh: 詔孫迥詳度行之。

translations.literal: Sun Jiong was ordered to review in detail and implement.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jiong was ordered to study the proposal and put it into effect.

sentences.zh: 知密州範鍔言：「板橋瀕海，東則二廣、福建、淮、浙，西則京東、河北、河東三路，商賈所聚，海舶之利顓於富家大姓。

translations.literal: Mizhou prefect Fan E said: " Banqiao lies on the sea; east are the two Guang, Fujian, Huai, and Zhe; west are the three circuits of Jingdong, Hebei, and Hedong—merchants gather; maritime profit concentrates in great wealthy clans.
translations.idiomatic: Mizhou prefect Fan E said, "Banqiao sits on the coast: to the east lie the two Guang, Fujian, Huai, and Zhe; to the west Jingdong, Hebei, and Hedong—merchants converge there, yet maritime profits stay in the hands of great wealthy houses—

sentences.zh: 宜即本州置市舶司，板橋鎮置抽解務。」

translations.literal: It is fitting immediately in this prefecture to set a Maritime Trade Office and at Banqiao town a collection-and-transit office."
translations.idiomatic: a Maritime Trade Office should be established in this prefecture and a collection depot at Banqiao town."

sentences.zh: 六年，詔都轉運使吳居厚條析以聞。

translations.literal: Year 6, Metropolitan Transport Commissioner Wu Juho was ordered to itemize and report.
translations.idiomatic: In 1083 Metropolitan Transport Commissioner Wu Juho was ordered to draft a detailed report.

sentences.zh: 元祐三年，鍔等復言：「廣南、福建、淮、浙賈人，航海販物至京東、河北、河東等路，運載錢帛絲綿貿易，而象犀、乳香珍異之物，雖嘗禁榷，未免欺隱。

translations.literal: Yuanyou year 3, Fan E and others again said: " Merchants of Guangnan, Fujian, Huai, and Zhe sail to sell goods in Jingdong, Hebei, Hedong, and other circuits, carrying cash, silks, and floss to trade; yet ivory, rhinoceros horn, frankincense, and rare goods—though once forbidden monopoly—still cannot avoid concealment.
translations.idiomatic: In 1088 Fan E and others renewed their plea: "Merchants from the south, Fujian, Huai, and Zhe sail north to Jingdong, Hebei, and Hedong with cash and silk, while ivory, frankincense, and other restricted luxuries are still smuggled despite the monopoly—

sentences.zh: 若板橋市舶法行，則海外諸物積於府庫者，必倍於杭、明二州。

translations.literal: If Banqiao maritime law is enacted, foreign goods accumulated in government stores will surely double Hang and Ming's two prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: if Banqiao's maritime office operates, state stores will hold twice what Hangzhou and Mingzhou now gather.

sentences.zh: 使商舶通行，無冒禁罹刑之患，而上供之物，免道路風水之虞。」

translations.literal: Let merchant ships pass freely, without the affliction of violating bans and suffering punishment; tribute goods would escape road and wind-and-water perils."
translations.idiomatic: Ships could sail openly without fear of smuggling penalties, and tribute goods would escape the hazards of overland transport.

sentences.zh: 乃置密州板橋市舶司。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Mizhou Banqiao Maritime Trade Office was established.
translations.idiomatic: The Mizhou Banqiao Maritime Trade Office was then established.

sentences.zh: 而前一年，亦增置市舶司於泉州。

translations.literal: The year before, a maritime office had also been added at Quanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The previous year a maritime office had also been added at Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 賈人由海道往外蕃，令以物貨名數並所詣之地，報所在州召保，毋得參帶兵器或可造兵器及違禁之物，官給以券。

translations.literal: Merchants going by sea route to outer fan were ordered to report goods' names and counts and their destination to the local prefecture for guarantors; they might not mix in weapons or weapon-making materials or banned goods—the office issued passes.
translations.idiomatic: Merchants sailing overseas had to declare cargo and destination to their prefecture and obtain guarantors; weapons, weapon-making materials, and contraband were forbidden—the state issued permits.

sentences.zh: 擅乘船由海入界河及往高麗、新羅、登萊州境者，罪以徒，往北界者加等。

translations.literal: Those who on their own took ships from the sea into boundary rivers or went to Koryŏ, Silla, or Deng-Lai borders were punished with penal servitude; toward the northern marches the penalty increased a grade.
translations.idiomatic: Unauthorized entry by sea into border rivers or voyages to Koryŏ, Silla, or Deng-Lai brought penal servitude; penalties increased for the northern frontier.

sentences.zh: 崇寧元年，復置杭、明市舶司，官吏如舊額。

translations.literal: Chongning year 1, Hang and Ming maritime offices were restored; clerks and officials as the old quotas.
translations.idiomatic: In 1102 the Hangzhou and Mingzhou maritime offices were restored with their former staffing.

sentences.zh: 三年，令蕃商欲往他郡者，從舶司給券，毋雜禁物、奸人。

translations.literal: Year 3, fan merchants wishing to go to other commanderies were to receive passes from the maritime office—no mixing forbidden goods or treacherous persons.
translations.idiomatic: In 1104 foreign merchants traveling to other prefectures had to obtain passes from the maritime office, without contraband or suspicious companions.

sentences.zh: 初，廣南舶司言，海外蕃商至廣州貿易，聽其往還居止，而大食諸國商亦丐通入他州及京東販易，故有是詔。

translations.literal: Earlier the Guangnan maritime office said overseas fan merchants coming to Guangzhou to trade were allowed to come and go and dwell; Dashi and other states' merchants also begged passage into other prefectures and Jingdong to trade—hence this edict.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Guangzhou had allowed foreign merchants to reside and travel freely; Arab and other traders had petitioned to trade in other prefectures and Jingdong—hence the edict.

sentences.zh: 凡海舶欲至福建、兩浙販易者，廣南舶司給防船兵仗，如詣諸國法。

translations.literal: All seagoing ships wishing to trade in Fujian or the two Zhe—the Guangnan maritime office supplied escort ships, troops, and arms, as with voyages to the various states.
translations.idiomatic: Ships bound for Fujian or the two Zhe circuits received armed escorts from Guangzhou, as for overseas voyages.

sentences.zh: 廣南舶司鬻所市物貨，取息毋過二分。

translations.literal: The Guangnan maritime office sold goods it had purchased; interest taken might not exceed two parts in a hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Guangzhou resold state-purchased goods at no more than two percent markup.

sentences.zh: 政和三年，詔如至道之法，凡知州、通判、官吏並舶司、使臣等，毋得市蕃商香藥、禁物。

translations.literal: Zhenghe year 3, an edict followed Zhidao-era law: all prefects, vice-prefects, clerks, maritime-office staff, and envoys might not buy fan merchants' aromatics or forbidden goods.
translations.idiomatic: In 1113, following Zhidao-era rules, prefects, vice-prefects, maritime staff, and envoys were forbidden to purchase foreign aromatics or restricted goods from merchants.

sentences.zh: 宣和元年，秀州開修青龍江浦，舶船輻輳，請復置監官。

translations.literal: Xuanhe year 1, Xiuzhou opened and repaired the Qinglong River estuary; merchant ships clustered thickly—they requested restoring supervisory officials.
translations.idiomatic: In 1119 Xiuzhou dredged the Qinglong River mouth; with ships crowding the harbor, officials asked to restore dedicated supervisors.

sentences.zh: 先是，政和中，置務設官於華亭縣，後江浦湮塞，蕃舶鮮至，止令縣官兼掌。

translations.literal: Earlier, in Zhenghe, an office and officials were set at Huating county; later the river mouth silted shut, fan ships rarely came—only county officials were left to manage concurrently.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhenghe an office had been set up at Huating, but after the estuary silted up foreign ships seldom called and county magistrates handled matters alone.

sentences.zh: 至是，復設官專領焉。

translations.literal: Now dedicated officials were again set to lead it exclusively.
translations.idiomatic: Dedicated supervisors were now restored.

sentences.zh: 四年，蕃國進奉物，如元豐法，令舶司即其地鬻之，毋發至京師，違者論罪。

translations.literal: Year 4, fan states' tribute goods, per Yuankeng law, were ordered sold on the spot by the maritime office—not sent to the capital; violators were punished.
translations.idiomatic: In 1122, per Yuankeng rules, foreign tribute goods were to be sold locally by the maritime office, not forwarded to the capital—violators were prosecuted.

sentences.zh: 契丹在太祖時，雖聽緣邊市易，而未有官署。

translations.literal: The Khitan under Taizu, though border markets were permitted, had no official agency.
translations.idiomatic: Under Song Taizu the Khitan were allowed frontier trade but no official market agency existed.

sentences.zh: 太平興國二年，始令鎮、易、雄、霸、滄州各置榷務，輦香藥、犀象及茶與交易。

translations.literal: Taiping Xingguo year 2, Zhen, Yi, Xiong, Ba, and Cang prefectures were first ordered each to set monopoly bureaus, carting aromatics, rhinoceros horn, ivory, and tea to exchange.
translations.idiomatic: In 977 Zhen, Yi, Xiong, Ba, and Cang prefectures each gained monopoly bureaus trading aromatics, ivory, and tea with the Khitan.

sentences.zh: 後有范陽之師，罷不與通。

translations.literal: Later came the Fanyang campaign; exchange was ended and they were not communicated with.
translations.idiomatic: After the Fanyang campaign, trade was cut off.

sentences.zh: 雍熙三年，禁河北商民與之貿易。

translations.literal: Yongxi year 3, Hebei merchants and commoners were forbidden to trade with them.
translations.idiomatic: In 986 Hebei merchants were forbidden to trade with them.

sentences.zh: 時累年興師，千里饋糧，居民疲乏，太宗亦頗有厭兵之意。

translations.literal: At the time armies were raised year after year; grain was supplied a thousand li; residents were weary and spent—Taizong too had considerable weariness of war.
translations.idiomatic: Years of campaigning had exhausted the people with supply lines stretching a thousand li, and Taizong himself had grown weary of war.

sentences.zh: 端拱元年，詔曰：「朕受命上穹，居尊中土，惟思禁暴，豈欲窮兵？

translations.literal: Duangong year 1, an edict said: " We received mandate from the upper vault, dwell in honor in the central land, only think to restrain violence—how could We desire to exhaust armies?
translations.idiomatic: In 988 an edict declared, "Heaven gave Us the mandate; We rule the central realm seeking only to curb violence—why would We crave endless war?

sentences.zh: 至於幽薊之民，皆吾赤子，宜許邊疆互相市易。

translations.literal: As for the people of You and Ji, all are Our red infants—frontier mutual markets should be permitted.
translations.idiomatic: The people of You and Ji are Our children; the frontier should be allowed mutual trade.

sentences.zh: 自今緣邊戍兵，不得輒恣侵略。」

translations.literal: From now border garrison troops must not rashly indulge in aggression and invasion."
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth border garrisons must not raid at will."

sentences.zh: 未幾復禁，違者抵死，北界商旅輒入內地販易，所在捕斬之。

translations.literal: Before long the ban was restored; violators faced death. Northern-border merchants who rashly entered the interior to trade were wherever encountered seized and beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the ban returned—violators faced death. Northern traders who slipped inland to sell were captured and executed wherever found.

sentences.zh: 淳化二年，令雄、霸州、靜戎軍、代州雁門砦置榷署如舊制，所鬻物增蘇木，尋復罷。

translations.literal: Chunhua year 2, Xiong and Ba prefectures, Jingrong Army, and Daizhou Yanmen Fort were ordered to set monopoly offices as the old system; goods sold added sappanwood—soon they were again abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In 991 monopoly offices were restored at Xiong, Ba, Jingrong Army, and Yanmen Fort, with sappanwood added to the trade list—then soon abolished again.

sentences.zh: 咸平五年，契丹求復置署，朝議以其翻覆，不許。

translations.literal: Xianping year 5, the Khitan asked to restore the offices; court discussion, because of their reversals, did not permit.
translations.idiomatic: In 1002 the Khitan sought to reopen the markets, but court debate cited their unreliability and refused.

sentences.zh: 知雄州何承矩繼請，乃聽置於雄州；

translations.literal: Xiongzhou prefect He Chengju petitioned again—then they were allowed at Xiongzhou;
translations.idiomatic: Xiongzhou prefect He Chengju pressed the case, and a market was allowed at Xiongzhou;

sentences.zh: 六年，罷。

translations.literal: year 6, abolished.
translations.idiomatic: in 1003 it was closed again.

sentences.zh: 景德初，復通好，請商賈即新城貿易。

translations.literal: Early Jingde, good relations were restored; they asked that merchants trade at the new city.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jingde era (1004–1007) relations warmed, and the Khitan asked that merchants trade at the new frontier city.

sentences.zh: 詔北商齎物貨至境上則許之。

translations.literal: An edict: northern merchants bringing goods to the border were then permitted.
translations.idiomatic: An edict allowed northern merchants to trade once they reached the border with goods in hand.

sentences.zh: 二年，令雄、霸州、安肅軍置三榷場，北商趨他路者，勿與為市。

translations.literal: Year 2, Xiong and Ba prefectures and Ansujun Army were ordered to set three monopoly markets; northern merchants who rushed to other routes were not given trade.
translations.idiomatic: In 1005 three monopoly markets were set at Xiong, Ba, and Ansujun; northern merchants using other routes were denied trade.

sentences.zh: 遣都官員外郎孔揆等乘傳詣三榷場，與轉運使劉綜並所在長吏平互市物價，稍優其直予之。

translations.literal: Palace Board Vice Director Kong Kui and others were sent by post relay to the three monopoly markets, with Transport Commissioner Liu Zong and local chief officials to balance mutual-market prices, slightly favoring their value in payment.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Board Vice Director Kong Kui and others were dispatched to the three markets with Transport Commissioner Liu Zong and local officials to set fair prices, paying the Khitan slightly above market rates.

sentences.zh: 又於廣信軍置場，皆廷臣專掌，通判兼領焉。

translations.literal: Another market was set at Guangxin Army; all were led exclusively by court appointees, with vice-prefects concurrently in charge.
translations.idiomatic: A fourth market was added at Guangxin Army, each run by a court-appointed commissioner with the vice-prefect as concurrent supervisor.

sentences.zh: 三年，詔民以書籍赴沿邊榷場博易者，非《九經》書疏悉禁之。

translations.literal: Year 3, an edict: commoners who brought books to frontier monopoly markets for exchange trade—all except the Nine Classics and their commentaries were forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: In 1006 the court barred civilians from trading books at the border markets except for the Nine Classics and standard commentaries.

sentences.zh: 凡官鬻物如舊，而增繒帛、漆器、粳糯，所入者有銀錢、布、羊馬、橐駝，歲獲四十餘萬。

translations.literal: All government-sold goods were as before, but silk, lacquerware, and husked rice were added; what came in included silver cash, cloth, sheep, horses, and camels, with yearly receipts of more than four hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: State sales continued as before, with added silk, lacquerware, and polished rice; Khitan payments in silver, cloth, livestock, and camels yielded annual revenue exceeding four hundred thousand strings.

sentences.zh: 天聖中，知雄州張昭遠請歲會入中金錢，仁宗曰：「先朝置互市以通有無，非以計利。」

translations.literal: In the Tiansheng era, Xiong Prefecture prefect Zhang Zhaoyuan requested that yearly accounts of gold and silver be sent to the capital; Emperor Renzong said: "Former emperors established mutual markets to circulate surpluses and shortages, not to calculate profit."
translations.idiomatic: During the Tiansheng reign (1023–1032) Zhang Zhaoyuan, prefect of Xiongzhou, asked that border-trade silver be remitted yearly to court; Renzong replied, "Our forebears opened these markets to balance want and plenty, not to turn a profit.

sentences.zh: 不許。

translations.literal: Permission was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: The request was denied.

sentences.zh: 終仁宗、英宗之世，契丹固守盟好，互市不絕。

translations.literal: Through the reigns of Renzong and Yingzong, the Khitan firmly kept the alliance, and mutual markets never ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout the reigns of Renzong and Yingzong the Khitan honored the treaty and frontier trade never lapsed.

sentences.zh: 熙寧八年，市易司請假奉宸庫象、犀、珠直總二十萬緡，於榷場貿易，明年終償之。

translations.literal: Xining year 8, the Market Exchange Office requested to borrow from the Fengchen Treasury ivory, rhinoceros horn, and pearls worth altogether two hundred thousand strings, to trade at monopoly markets and repay in full the next year.
translations.idiomatic: In 1075 the Market Exchange Office asked to borrow two hundred thousand strings' worth of ivory, rhinoceros horn, and pearls from the imperial treasury for border-market trade, promising full repayment the following year.

sentences.zh: 詔許。

translations.literal: An edict permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved the loan.

sentences.zh: 九年，立與化外人私貿易罪賞法。

translations.literal: Year 9, established a law on crimes and rewards for private trade with foreigners.
translations.idiomatic: In 1076 the state codified penalties and rewards for unauthorized trade with foreigners.

sentences.zh: 河北四榷場，自治平四年，其貨物專掌於三司之催轄司，而度支賞給案判官置簿督計之。

translations.literal: The four Hebei monopoly markets, since Zhiping year 4, had their goods exclusively managed by the Three Departments' Cuixia Office, while the Revenue Section's reward-and-grant case judge kept ledgers to supervise accounts.
translations.idiomatic: Since 1067 the four Hebei border markets had been run by the Three Departments' procurement office, with Revenue Section clerks keeping the accounts.

sentences.zh: 至是，以私販者眾，故有是命。

translations.literal: At this point, because private traders were numerous, there was this order.
translations.idiomatic: Smuggling had grown so widespread that the new statute was issued.

sentences.zh: 未幾，又禁私市硫黃、焰硝及以盧甘石入他界者，河東亦如之。

translations.literal: Before long, private sale of sulfur and saltpeter and bringing alum into other territories were also banned; Hedong followed likewise.
translations.idiomatic: Soon private sales of sulfur, saltpeter, and alum across the border were banned as well, with identical rules in Hedong.

sentences.zh: 元豐元年，復申賣書北界告捕之法。

translations.literal: Yuanfeng year 1, again announced the law on selling books to the northern border with reporting and arrest.
translations.idiomatic: In 1078 the court again enforced the rule requiring informants and arrests for selling books to the Khitan frontier.

sentences.zh: 西夏自景德四年，於保安軍置榷場，以繒帛、羅綺易駝馬、牛羊、玉、氈毯、甘草，以香藥、瓷漆器、薑桂等物易蜜蠟、麝臍、毛褐、原羚角、碙砂、柴胡、蓯蓉、紅花、翎毛，非官市者聽與民交易，入貢至京者縱其為市。

translations.literal: Western Xia, since Jingde year 4, set a monopoly market at Bao'an Army, exchanging silk and gauze for camels, horses, cattle, sheep, jade, felt rugs, and licorice; exchanging aromatics, porcelain, lacquerware, ginger, cinnamon, and the like for beeswax, musk navel, woolen cloth, antelope horn, sal ammoniac, bupleurum, cistanche, safflower, and feathers; outside official markets, private trade with the people was permitted, and those who came to the capital as tribute were allowed to trade freely.
translations.idiomatic: Since 1007 the Tanguts had traded at a licensed market in Bao'an: Song silk and brocade for livestock, jade, felt, and licorice; spices, ceramics, and ginger for wax, musk, wool, medicines, safflower, and plumes. Private dealings were allowed alongside the official exchange, and tribute envoys reaching the capital could trade at will.

sentences.zh: 天聖中，陝西榷場二、並代路亦請置場和市，許之。

translations.literal: In the Tiansheng era, two Shaanxi monopoly markets were set, and the Bingdai Circuit also requested markets for harmonized trade; it was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: During Tiansheng two more Shaanxi markets opened, and Bingdai Circuit's request for additional harmonized-trade posts was granted.

sentences.zh: 及元昊反，即詔陝西、河東絕其互市，廢保安軍榷場；

translations.literal: When Yuan Hao rebelled, an edict at once cut off mutual markets in Shaanxi and Hedong and abolished the Bao'an Army monopoly market;
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Hao rebelled, the court severed frontier trade in Shaanxi and Hedong and closed the Bao'an market;

sentences.zh: 後又禁陝西並邊主兵官與屬羌交易。

translations.literal: Later, trade between Shaanxi frontier commanders and dependent Qiang was also forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: commanders along the Shaanxi frontier were later forbidden to trade with allied Qiang tribes as well.

sentences.zh: 久之，元昊請臣，數遣使求復互市。

translations.literal: After a long time, Yuan Hao submitted as a subject and repeatedly sent envoys seeking restoration of mutual markets.
translations.idiomatic: Eventually Yuan Hao submitted and sent repeated embassies asking to reopen the markets.

sentences.zh: 慶曆六年，復為置場於保安、鎮戎二軍。

translations.literal: Qingli year 6, markets were again set at the two armies of Bao'an and Zhenrong.
translations.idiomatic: In 1046 markets were restored at Bao'an and Zhenrong.

sentences.zh: 繼言驅馬羊至，無放牧之地，為徙保安軍榷場於順寧砦。

translations.literal: They then said that when horses and sheep were driven there, there was no pastureland, so the Bao'an Army monopoly market was moved to Shunning Fort.
translations.idiomatic: The Tanguts complained that herds brought to trade had no grazing ground, so the Bao'an market was relocated to Shunning Fort.

sentences.zh: 既而蕃商卒無至者。

translations.literal: Before long, Tangut merchants in the end did not come.
translations.idiomatic: Tangut traders soon stopped coming altogether.

sentences.zh: 嘉祐初，西人侵耕屈野河地，知并州龐籍謂：「非絕其互市，則內侵不已。

translations.literal: Early Jiayou, westerners encroached on farming the Quye River lands; Bing Prefecture prefect Pang Ji said: "Unless their mutual markets are cut off, inward encroachment will not cease.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jiayou era (1056–1063) Tanguts began farming disputed land along the Quye River; Bingzhou prefect Pang Ji argued, "Only by shutting down trade can we stop their steady push inward.

sentences.zh: 且聞出兀臧訛龐之謀，若互市不通，其國必歸罪訛龐，年歲間，然後可與計議。」

translations.literal: Moreover it was heard that this came from the plot of Wu Zang E Pang; if mutual markets do not flow, their state will surely blame E Pang, and within a year or two negotiation can then be undertaken."
translations.idiomatic: This encroachment, I hear, is the work of the minister Wu Zang E Pang. Cut off trade and his own court will blame him; within a year or two we can negotiate from strength.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: It was followed.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 初，第禁陝西四路私與西人貿易，未幾，乃悉絕之。

translations.literal: At first, only private trade between the four Shaanxi routes and westerners was banned; before long, all trade was cut off entirely.
translations.idiomatic: At first only private trade along the four Shaanxi circuits was banned; soon every channel of exchange was closed.

sentences.zh: 治平四年，河東經略司言，西界乞通和市。

translations.literal: Zhiping year 4, the Hedong frontier commission reported that the western realm begged to open harmonized markets.
translations.idiomatic: In 1067 the Hedong frontier command reported that the Tanguts were asking to reopen harmonized trade.

sentences.zh: 自夏人攻慶州大順城，詔罷歲賜，嚴禁邊民無得私相貿易。

translations.literal: Since the Xia people attacked Qingzhou's Dashun City, an edict halted the yearly gifts and strictly forbade border people from private mutual trade.
translations.idiomatic: After the Tanguts attacked Dashuncheng in Qingzhou, the court suspended annual gifts and strictly forbade any private border trade.

sentences.zh: 至是，上章謝罪，乃復許之。

translations.literal: At this point they submitted a memorial apologizing, and trade was again permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Now, having submitted an apology, they were allowed to trade again.

sentences.zh: 後二年，令涇原熟戶及河東、陝西邊民勿與通市。

translations.literal: Two years later, Jingyuan acculturated households and Hedong and Shaanxi border people were ordered not to trade with them.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later acculturated households in Jingyuan and civilians in Hedong and Shaanxi were forbidden to deal with the Tanguts.

sentences.zh: 又二年，因回使議立和市，而私販不能止，遂申詔諸路禁絕。

translations.literal: Another two years later, through a Hui envoy harmonized markets were discussed, but private trade could not be stopped, so an edict was announced forbidding trade on all routes.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later a Hui envoy negotiated reopening the markets, yet smuggling continued until the court banned trade on every frontier route.

sentences.zh: 既而河東轉運司請罷吳堡，於寧星和市如舊。
