translations.literal: Soon after, the Hedong transport commission requested abolishing Wubao and restoring harmonized trade at Ningxing as before.
translations.idiomatic: The Hedong transport office then asked to close Wubao and restore the old harmonized market at Ningxing.

sentences.zh: 而麟州復奏夏人之請，乃令鬻銅、錫以市馬，而纖縞與急須之物皆禁。

translations.literal: But Linzhou again memorialized the Xia people's request, so selling copper and tin for horses was ordered, while fine silks and urgently needed goods were all forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: When Linzhou reported another Tangut petition, the court allowed copper and tin for horses only, banning fine silks and other goods they urgently needed.

sentences.zh: 西北歲入馬，事具《兵志》。

translations.literal: Northwest yearly intake of horses—the matter is fully recorded in the Military Treatise.
translations.idiomatic: Annual horse purchases from the northwest are detailed in the Military Treatise.

sentences.zh: 建炎四年三月，宣撫使張浚奏，大食國遣人進珠玉寶貝。

translations.literal: Jianyan year 4, third month, Pacification Commissioner Zhang Jun memorialized that the Dashi kingdom sent people presenting pearls, jade, and treasures.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of 1130 Pacification Commissioner Zhang Jun reported that Arab envoys had arrived bearing pearls, jade, and curios.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「大觀、宣和間，川茶不以博馬，惟市珠玉，故武備不修，遂致危弱如此。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "During Daguan and Xuanhe, Sichuan tea was not used to trade for horses but only to buy pearls and jade, so military readiness was not maintained, leading to such weakness as this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Under Huizong we traded Sichuan tea for pearls and jade instead of horses, neglected our defenses, and brought the dynasty to this pass.

sentences.zh: 今復捐數十萬緡易無用之物，曷若惜財以養戰士乎？」

translations.literal: Now again throwing away several hundred thousand strings for useless things—how is that better than cherishing wealth to nourish warriors?"
translations.idiomatic: Why spend another few hundred thousand strings on trinkets when that silver could feed our soldiers?"

sentences.zh: 諭張浚勿受，量賜予以答之。

translations.literal: He instructed Zhang Jun not to accept them and to measure out gifts in reply.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun was told to decline the tribute and reply with a modest gift in kind.

sentences.zh: 六月，罷宜州歲市朱砂二萬兩。

translations.literal: Sixth month, the yearly Yizhou market purchase of twenty thousand liang of cinnabar was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: That sixth month the court ended Yizhou's annual purchase of twenty thousand taels of cinnabar.

sentences.zh: 紹興三年，邕州守臣言大理請入貢。

translations.literal: Shaoxing year 3, the Yongzhou frontier official reported that Dali requested to enter tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In 1133 the Yongzhou prefect reported that Dali wished to send tribute.

sentences.zh: 上諭大臣，止令賣馬，不許其進貢。

translations.literal: The emperor instructed the ministers: only allow them to sell horses; do not permit them to present tribute.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told his ministers to permit only horse sales and to reject any formal tribute mission.

sentences.zh: 四年，詔川、陝即永興軍、威茂州置博易場；

translations.literal: Year 4, an edict ordered Sichuan and Shaanxi to set exchange markets at Yongxing Army and Weimao Prefecture;
translations.idiomatic: In 1134 edicts established exchange markets at Yongxing Army and Weimao in Sichuan and Shaanxi;

sentences.zh: 移廣西買馬司於邕管，歲捐金帛，倍酬其直。

translations.literal: the Guangxi Horse Purchase Office was moved to the Yong prefecture circuit, yearly donating gold and silks, paying double their value.
translations.idiomatic: and relocated the Guangxi Horse Purchase Office to Yongzhou, paying double market price in annual silk and silver.

sentences.zh: 然言語不通，一聽譯者高下其手，吏得因緣為奸。

translations.literal: Yet languages did not communicate; everything was left to interpreters raising or lowering their hands, and clerks could use the opportunity for fraud.
translations.idiomatic: But with no common language, interpreters fixed prices at will and officials found endless chances for graft.

sentences.zh: 六年，大理國獻象及馬五百匹，詔償其馬直，卻象勿受，而賜書勞遣之。

translations.literal: Year 6, the Dali kingdom presented elephants and five hundred horses; an edict compensated the horse price, declined the elephants and did not accept them, and bestowed a letter of comfort to dismiss them.
translations.idiomatic: In 1136 Dali sent elephants and five hundred horses; the court paid for the horses, refused the elephants, and sent a letter of thanks dismissing the embassy.

sentences.zh: 十二年，盱眙軍置榷場官監，與北商博易，淮西、京西、陝西榷場亦如之。

translations.literal: Year 12, Xuyi Army set monopoly-market official supervisors to exchange trade with northern merchants; Huai west, Jing west, and Shaanxi monopoly markets were likewise.
translations.idiomatic: In 1142 Xuyi Army gained a supervised border market for Jurchen traders, and similar markets opened in Huai west, Jingxi, and Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 十九年，罷國信所博易。

translations.literal: Year 19, the Guoxin Office exchange trade was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In 1149 the Guoxin Office's exchange trade was shut down.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，罷廉州貢珠，散蜑丁。

translations.literal: Year 26, Lianzhou pearl tribute was abolished and Dan boatmen were dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: In 1156 the court ended Lianzhou's pearl tribute and disbanded the Dan divers.

sentences.zh: 蓋珠池之在廉州凡十餘，按交阯者水深百尺，而大珠生焉。

translations.literal: For pearl pools at Lianzhou numbered more than ten; according to Jiaozhi, the water was a hundred chi deep, and large pearls were born there.
translations.idiomatic: Lianzhou held more than a dozen pearl beds; off Jiaozhi the water ran a hundred feet deep and the finest pearls grew there.

sentences.zh: 蜑往采之，多為交人所取，又為大魚所害。

translations.literal: The Dan went to harvest them, but many were taken by Jiao people, and they were also harmed by large fish.
translations.idiomatic: When the Dan divers went out, Vietnamese raiders seized their catch and great fish took many lives.

sentences.zh: 至是，罷之。

translations.literal: At this point, it was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The fishery was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，存盱眙軍榷場，餘並罷。

translations.literal: Year 29, only the Xuyi Army monopoly market was kept; the rest were all abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In 1159 only the Xuyi market survived; all others were closed.

sentences.zh: 乾道元年，襄陽鄧城鎮、壽春花靨鎮、光州光山縣中渡市皆置榷場，以守臣措置，通判提轄。

translations.literal: Qiandao year 1, Xiangyang's Dengcheng Town, Shouchun's Huayan Town, and Guangzhou Guangshan County's Zhongdu Market all set monopoly markets, arranged by frontier officials with vice-prefects supervising.
translations.idiomatic: In 1165 monopoly markets opened at Dengcheng in Xiangyang, Huayan in Shouchun, and Zhongdu in Guangshan, each run by the local prefect with a vice-prefect as supervisor.

sentences.zh: 五年，省提轄官。

translations.literal: Year 5, the supervising officials were cut.
translations.idiomatic: In 1169 the dedicated supervisor posts were abolished.

sentences.zh: 淳熙二年，臣僚言：溪峒緣邊州縣置博易場，官主之。

translations.literal: Chunxi year 2, officials said: stream-gorge frontier prefectures and counties set exchange markets with officials presiding.
translations.idiomatic: In 1175 officials noted that exchange markets along the stream-gorge frontier were run directly by the state.

sentences.zh: 七年，塞外諸戎販珠玉入黎州，官常邀市之。

translations.literal: Year 7, outer barbarians beyond the passes sold pearls and jade into Lizhou; officials often intercepted them for forced purchase.
translations.idiomatic: In 1180 tribes beyond the passes brought pearls and jade to Lizhou, where officials routinely forced preemptive purchases.

sentences.zh: 臣僚言其黷貨啟釁，非便，止合聽商賈、百姓收買。

translations.literal: Officials said this corrupt seizure of goods provoked incidents and was not convenient; they should only let merchants and commoners buy.
translations.idiomatic: Officials warned that official buying bred corruption and border incidents, and urged that only merchants and civilians be allowed to purchase.

sentences.zh: 詔從之。

translations.literal: An edict followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 建炎元年，詔：「市舶多以無用之物費國用，自今有博買篤耨香環、瑪瑙、貓兒眼睛之類，皆置於法；

translations.literal: Jianyan year 1, an edict: "Maritime trade often wastes state funds on useless goods; from now on state purchases of eaglewood rings, agate, cat's-eye stones, and the like are all placed under law;
translations.idiomatic: In 1127 an edict declared, "Maritime trade too often squanders treasury silver on luxuries. From now on state purchases of eaglewood rings, agate, cat's-eye, and similar goods are subject to statute;

sentences.zh: 惟宣賜臣僚象笏、犀帶，選可者輸送。」

translations.literal: only for imperial gifts to officials of ivory tablets and rhinoceros belts—select acceptable ones and deliver them.
translations.idiomatic: only ivory tablets and rhinoceros belts for imperial gifts to officials may be selected and forwarded."

sentences.zh: 胡人謂三百斤為一婆蘭，凡舶舟最大者曰獨檣，載一千婆蘭。

translations.literal: Foreigners call three hundred jin one po-lan; the largest merchant ships are called single-mast and carry one thousand po-lan.
translations.idiomatic: Foreign merchants called three hundred jin a po-lan; the largest ships, known as single-masters, carried a thousand po-lan.

sentences.zh: 次者曰牛頭，比獨檣得三之一。

translations.literal: The next size was called ox-head, one-third the capacity of a single-mast.
translations.idiomatic: The next class, called ox-heads, carried one-third as much.

sentences.zh: 又次曰木舶，曰料河，遞得三之一。

translations.literal: Still smaller were called timber ships and liao-he, each again one-third.
translations.idiomatic: Smaller still were timber ships and liao-he vessels, each again one-third the size below.

sentences.zh: 隆興二年，臣僚言：「熙寧初，立市舶以通物貨。

translations.literal: Longxing year 2, officials said: "Early Xining, maritime trade offices were established to circulate goods.
translations.idiomatic: In 1164 officials reminded the throne, "When the maritime trade system was founded in the Xining era,

sentences.zh: 舊法抽解有定數，而取之不苛，輸稅寬其期，而使之待價，懷遠之意實寓焉。

translations.literal: The old law fixed quotas for seizure but took without harshness, broadened the period for paying tax and let them await prices—the intent to cherish the distant was truly lodged therein.
translations.idiomatic: quotas were fixed but fairly assessed, taxes were deferred so merchants could wait for good prices—the policy truly embodied goodwill toward distant traders.

sentences.zh: 邇來抽解既多，又迫使之輸，致貨滯而價減。

translations.literal: Recently seizures have been numerous and merchants are also forced to pay at once, causing goods to stagnate and prices to fall.
translations.idiomatic: Lately seizures have multiplied and payment is demanded immediately, so goods pile up and prices collapse.

sentences.zh: 擇其良者，如犀角、象齒十分抽二，又博買四分；

translations.literal: Choosing the fine goods, such as rhinoceros horn and ivory: two-tenths seized, and another four-tenths state-purchased;
translations.idiomatic: On fine goods such as rhinoceros horn and ivory the state now takes two-tenths in quota seizure and buys another four-tenths;

sentences.zh: 珠十分抽一，又博買六分。

translations.literal: pearls: one-tenth seized, and another six-tenths state-purchased.
translations.idiomatic: on pearls one-tenth is seized and six-tenths forcibly purchased.

sentences.zh: 舶戶懼抽買數多，止買粗色雜貨。

translations.literal: Ship owners fearing numerous seizures and purchases now buy only coarse mixed goods.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing heavy seizures and state purchases, ship owners now carry only cheap mixed cargo.

sentences.zh: 若象齒、珠犀比他貨至重，乞十分抽一，更不博買。」

translations.literal: If ivory, pearls, and rhinoceros are heavier burdens than other goods, we beg one-tenth seizure only and no further state purchase."
translations.idiomatic: Ivory, pearls, and rhinoceros bear the heaviest burden—reduce the levy to one-tenth and end forced purchase altogether.

sentences.zh: 乾道二年，罷兩浙路提舉，以守倅及知縣、監官共事，轉運司提督之。

translations.literal: Qiandao year 2, the Liangzhe route commissioner was abolished; prefectural deputies, county magistrates, and supervisory officials worked together, with the transport office supervising.
translations.idiomatic: In 1166 the Liangzhe maritime commissioner was abolished; prefects, vice-prefects, magistrates, and port supervisors shared the work under transport-office oversight.

sentences.zh: 三年，詔廣南、兩浙市舶司所發舟還，因風水不便、船破檣壞者，即不得抽解。

translations.literal: Year 3, an edict: returning ships dispatched by the Guangnan and Liangzhe maritime trade offices that suffered inconvenient winds and waters or broken hulls and masts were at once not subject to seizure.
translations.idiomatic: In 1167 the court ruled that Guangnan and Liangzhe ships damaged by storms or wrecked on the return voyage were exempt from quota seizure.

sentences.zh: 七年，詔見任官以錢附綱首商旅過蕃買物者有罰，舶至除抽解和買，違法抑買者，許蕃商越訴，計贓罪之。

translations.literal: Year 7, an edict: incumbent officials who attached money to gang chiefs and merchants crossing to fan territories to buy goods would be punished; when ships arrived, aside from seizure and harmonized purchase, those who illegally suppressed buying were permitted to let fan merchants appeal over their heads, counting the stolen goods as crime.
translations.idiomatic: In 1171 officials who lent money to convoy leaders for overseas purchases faced penalties; beyond lawful seizure and state purchase, merchants could appeal over illegal price-fixing, with penalties based on the bribe's value.

sentences.zh: 舊法，細色綱龍腦、珠之類，每一綱五千兩，其餘犀象、紫礦、乳檀香之類，為粗色，每綱一萬斤。

translations.literal: Under the old law, fine-color convoys—dragon's brain, pearls, and the like—were five thousand liang per convoy; the rest, rhinoceros, ivory, purple ore, milk sandalwood, and the like, were coarse color, ten thousand jin per convoy.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old rules a fine-goods convoy of borneol, pearls, and the like was capped at five thousand taels; rhinoceros horn, ivory, purple ore, and sandalwood counted as coarse goods at ten thousand jin per convoy.

sentences.zh: 凡起一綱，遣衙前一名部送，支腳乘贍家錢一百餘緡。

translations.literal: Whenever a convoy was dispatched, one yamen runner was sent to escort it, paying travel and family-support money of a little more than one hundred strings.
translations.idiomatic: Each convoy required a yamen runner escort at a travel allowance of just over one hundred strings.

sentences.zh: 大觀以後，張大其數，象犀、紫礦皆作細色起發，以舊日一綱分為三十二綱，多費腳乘贍家錢三千餘貫。

translations.literal: After Daguan, the numbers were inflated; ivory, rhinoceros, and purple ore were all dispatched as fine color, splitting what had been one convoy into thirty-two convoys, spending more than three thousand strings on travel allowances.
translations.idiomatic: After the Daguan era (1107–1110) quotas ballooned: ivory, rhinoceros horn, and purple ore were reclassified as fine goods, one old convoy became thirty-two, and travel costs rose above three thousand strings.

sentences.zh: 至於乾道七年，詔廣南起發粗色香藥物貨，每綱二萬斤，加耗六百斤，依舊支破水腳錢一千六百六十二貫有奇。

translations.literal: By Qiandao year 7, an edict ordered Guangnan dispatch of coarse aromatics and goods at twenty thousand jin per convoy, with six hundred jin allowance for wastage, paying portage as before of one thousand six hundred sixty-two strings and a fraction.
translations.idiomatic: In 1171 Guangnan coarse aromatics were fixed at twenty thousand jin per convoy with a six-hundred-jin wastage allowance and portage pay of 1,662 strings and change, as under the old rule.

sentences.zh: 淳熙二年，戶部言：「福建、廣南市舶司粗細物貨，並以五萬斤為一全綱。」

translations.literal: Chunxi year 2, the Revenue Board said: "Fujian and Guangnan maritime trade offices' coarse and fine goods alike shall take fifty thousand jin as one full convoy."
translations.idiomatic: In 1175 the Revenue Board ruled that Fujian and Guangnan would treat both fine and coarse cargo as a single full convoy at fifty thousand jin.

sentences.zh: 南渡，三路舶司歲入固不少，然金銀銅鐵，海舶飛運，所失良多，而銅錢之泄尤甚。

translations.literal: After the southern crossing, the three-route maritime offices' yearly intake was indeed not small, yet gold, silver, copper, and iron were swiftly transported by sea ships, with very many losses, and the leakage of copper cash was especially severe.
translations.idiomatic: After the court fled south the three maritime commissions still collected substantial revenue, yet bullion and metals shipped overseas in vast quantities—and copper cash leaked abroad worst of all.

sentences.zh: 法禁雖嚴，奸巧愈密，商人貪利而貿遷，黠吏受賕而縱釋，其弊卒不可禁。

translations.literal: Though the laws and bans were strict, crafty evasions grew ever denser; merchants, greedy for profit, moved goods in trade, and clever clerks accepted bribes and released them—the abuses in the end could not be forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Bans grew stricter while smuggling grew subtler: merchants chased profit across the seas, clerks took bribes and looked away—and in the end the abuse could not be stopped.
